# Features — ai-gent docs site and runners

Status: Draft

The parts of ai-gent that are software with behavior: the documentation site (`docs/site/`) and the scripts that run things (installer, runners, planners). The skills themselves (`plugins/*/skills/**/SKILL.md` and their references) are their own specification and are not reconstructed here. Every feature was reverse-engineered from code at commit 384c771; statuses come from evidence only (see `docs/product/introspec.md`).

Sides: the docs site has only a Frontend; the runners are command-line tools with no UI, so their status is in the Backend column (the code path) and Frontend is N/A. QA is the end-to-end evidence: a suite that drives the real thing and runs in CI.

Verified needs suites covering every story, running and passing in CI; for tooling without a UI the integration suites stand in for e2e journeys (pipeline rule 6). 008 is Verified: its unit tests run on every pull request and the real-engine suite weekly. The closest others are 006 (all stories but the interactive selector) and 002 (two of four stories).

013–017 are forward specs (not reconstructed): optional Claude Code mods — hooks modules in the plugin they serve — that surface or enforce what the skills, scripts and guard hooks already guarantee, and are never part of a contract. For them, Frontend is what the person sees (pane, band, status line, toast, dialog, command output) and Backend is hook logic that gates or rewrites (tool calls, prompts) plus any script change. All depend on 012 (the checkpoint mod, specified and built on its own branch), which settles the module layout, `check.sh` wiring, versioning and install they reuse.

018–031 are the second set of forward mod specs (written 2026-10-31, now Implemented on `dev`; 024 story 3 and the remaining 029 runs are not built): each is read-only and optional like 013–017, and each lists its open questions as `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`. Decisions of 2026-10-31 settled every open question (see each spec's Decisions section). Prerequisite changes land first, each on its own branch: `token_report.py tasks --dry-run --json` (020, 014 story 5), `leftovers.sh --json` (025), `release.py` and `shared/release-single.py` `--json` (028), and the `skipIn: result` pattern flag with regenerated `secret-data.ts` (026). Also decided 2026-10-31: bands above the prompt obey a priority cap of two (specified in 030); releases are batched from `dev` in themed promotions; the work is built with `agents:orchestrate` in parallel worktrees after the specs are reviewed and accepted. Suggested build order, by what they unblock: 014 story 5 (`/tokens --live`, with `tasks --dry-run --json`) → 018 → 019 → 020; 026 (the only P1) with its shared-pattern change; 021 and 023; 024 and 027; then 022, 025 and 028. One branch per spec, landed on `dev` one at a time.


032-034 and 039 are the Rust and 3.0.0 planning set (written 2026-11-01 from `docs/product/rust-decisions.md`; the tools and docs-site specs 035-038 and 040 are in the same set). They are Backend/CLI features with no UI, so Frontend is N/A; each has spec, plan, tasks, data model, contracts and a quickstart or fixture description, so a session that stops leaves resumable work (D17). Their Status is Planned until a task is built and evidenced.

# Feature Specification: Docs site shell and generated content

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `docs/site/` — the layout every page shares, the content generated from the repository, the theme, the locale contract and the version footer.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Content generated from the repository (Priority: P1)

A maintainer runs any site command; the site's content (plugins, skills, versions, README, changelog) is regenerated from the repository it documents, so no page can drift from the skill files.

**Why this priority**: every other docs feature renders this content; truthfulness to code is the brief's first architecture driver.

**Independent Test**: run `bun run gen` and compare `src/content/generated.json` with `plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a plugin directory with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, **When** `bun run gen` runs, **Then** each `skills/<s>/SKILL.md` becomes one skill entry with id `<plugin>-<skill>`, its frontmatter `name` and `description`, its body and a source URL [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/generate-content.mjs:54-94].
2. **Given** a directory under `plugins/` with no manifest, **When** content is generated, **Then** it is skipped [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/generate-content.mjs:61].
3. **Given** the build runs on a release tag, **When** source links are generated, **Then** they point at that tag, else at the commit, else at `main` [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/generate-content.mjs:23; tests/content.test.ts:37].
4. **Given** `dev`, `build`, `test` or `typecheck` is run, **When** it starts, **Then** `gen` runs first [OBSERVED: docs/site/package.json scripts].

---

### User Story 2 - Version footer (Priority: P2)

A reader sees which toolkit and docs versions a page was built from, each linked to that tree.

**Why this priority**: readers and agents need to know whether the page matches the version they installed.

**Independent Test**: `tests/version.test.ts` and `tests/app.test.tsx` "shows each version in the footer".

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** HEAD is exactly tag `2.8.0`, **When** the site builds, **Then** the footer reads `ai-gent@v2.8.0 · docs@v<package.json version>` linked to `/tree/2.8.0` [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/version.mjs:37-48; tests/version.test.ts:13].
2. **Given** HEAD is past the last tag, **When** the site builds, **Then** both versions carry `+<short sha>` and link to the commit [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/version.mjs:41-43; tests/version.test.ts:25].
3. **Given** no tag and no git, **When** the site builds, **Then** the footer reads `ai-gent@dev` with no link [OBSERVED: tests/version.test.ts:37].

---

### User Story 3 - Theme choice (Priority: P2)

A reader switches between dark and light themes from the footer; the choice persists across visits. Dark is the default.

**Why this priority**: the UX vision's dark-first direction; accessibility of contrast in both themes.

**Independent Test**: `tests/app.test.tsx` "switches the theme from the footer's icon buttons".

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** no stored choice, **When** the page loads, **Then** `data-theme="dark"` is set before render [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/main.tsx:6-9].
2. **Given** the reader presses the sun button, **When** the theme changes, **Then** it is stored under `ai-gent-docs-theme` and the button is `aria-pressed` [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/components.tsx:36-67].

---

### User Story 4 - Locale contract (Priority: P3)

A contributor can add a locale as a content task: every registered locale must be a complete `Messages` set, and the locale switcher appears only once a second locale exists.

**Why this priority**: the brief keeps the i18n architecture although only en-US ships.

**Independent Test**: `tests/i18n.test.tsx`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `LOCALES = ["en-US"]`, **When** the top bar renders, **Then** no locale switcher is shown [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/i18n.tsx:9; docs/site/src/components.tsx:106].
2. **Given** a stored or browser-preferred locale, **When** the app starts, **Then** a supported one is chosen, else the first locale, and the choice persists under `ai-gent-docs-locale` [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/i18n.tsx:403-445; tests/i18n.test.tsx:37].
3. **Given** a locale missing a key, **When** tests run, **Then** the completeness test fails [OBSERVED: tests/i18n.test.tsx:28].

---

### User Story 5 - Shared layout, navigation and metadata (Priority: P1)

Every page has a skip link, a top bar with the primary sections (desktop links, a mobile menu), a footer with versions, license and theme, and HTML metadata for previews and LLM discovery.

**Why this priority**: the frame of every page and every link preview.

**Independent Test**: `tests/app.test.tsx`, `tests/meta.test.ts`, axe checks in `tests/pages.test.tsx`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** any route, **When** it renders, **Then** the top bar links Install, Skills, Flow, Contribute, Reference and Changelog, with a mobile menu toggled by an `aria-expanded` button [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/components.tsx:125-200].
2. **Given** the built `index.html`, **When** it is served, **Then** it advertises `og:image` (1200×630), a Twitter large card, a canonical URL and `llms.txt` as an alternate [OBSERVED: docs/site/index.html:11-39; tests/meta.test.ts:11-27].
3. **Given** the footer, **When** it renders, **Then** it shows GPL v3+ linked to `LICENSE` at the build's ref [OBSERVED: tests/app.test.tsx:22].

### Edge Cases

- The skip link is `href="#main"` inside a `HashRouter`: activating it changes the hash route to `main`, which matches no route [INFERRED: docs/site/src/components.tsx:376 + docs/site/src/App.tsx:21-31 → the skip link likely renders the not-found page instead of moving focus; confirm with a keyboard test in a browser].
- A `SKILL.md` frontmatter value spanning several lines is read only up to the first line; the generator's parser is line-based [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/generate-content.mjs:36-45]. Descriptions are single-line by repository rule, so this holds today.
- Personal skills under `skills/` (`skill-docs`) aren't in the site; only plugin skills are generated [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/generate-content.mjs:49].
- The copy button announces "Copied" even when the clipboard write failed [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/components.tsx:232-240].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The build MUST generate `src/content/generated.json` from `plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md`, plus `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/generate-content.mjs:96-109].
- **FR-002**: The generated file MUST NOT be hand-edited; it is gitignored [OBSERVED: CLAUDE.md "Docs site"].
- **FR-003**: The footer MUST show the toolkit and docs versions per US2.
- **FR-004**: The theme MUST default to dark and persist the reader's choice.
- **FR-005**: Every locale in `LOCALES` MUST be a complete `Messages` set; the switcher MUST be hidden with one locale.
- **FR-006**: The site MUST be served under a path prefix taken from `VITE_BASE_PATH` (default `/ai-gent/`) and use hash routing [OBSERVED: docs/site/vite.config.ts:7; docs/site/src/App.tsx:19].
- **FR-007**: Pages MUST pass axe checks (landing, flow, skill page) [OBSERVED: tests/pages.test.tsx:40,70,88].

### Key Entities

- **Plugin**, **Skill**, **Version** — see `data-model.md`.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Every plugin skill in the repository has exactly one generated entry with a unique id [OBSERVED: tests/content.test.ts:13-23].
- **SC-002**: Zero axe violations on the tested pages [OBSERVED: tests/pages.test.tsx].
- **SC-003**: The footer version equals `git describe` at build time.

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: the skip link's behavior under hash routing was never checked in a browser; the e2e smoke doesn't exercise it.]
- [ASSUMPTION: personal skills (`skills/`) are deliberately left out of the site.]

# Feature Specification: Skill finder and skill reference

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `docs/site/src/pages.tsx` (LandingPage, SkillsPage, SkillPage, NotFoundPage), `docs/site/src/components.tsx` (SearchBox, SkillIndex, SkillRow) and `docs/site/src/content.ts`.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Open a skill's page and copy its invoke command (Priority: P1)

A toolkit user opens `#/use/skills/<plugin>-<skill>` and gets the skill's description, how to invoke it in Claude Code and in the other agents, its trigger phrases, the full SKILL.md body, its source link and the plugin's other skills.

**Why this priority**: the UX vision's first principle — "the skill page is the product".

**Independent Test**: `tests/pages.test.tsx` "renders a skill page with its invoke command"; the e2e smoke opens `#/use/skills/qa-load`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** skill `qa-load`, **When** its page opens, **Then** it shows `/qa:load` for Claude Code and `/qa-load` for opencode and Cursor (`$qa-load` in Codex) in a copyable block [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/pages.tsx:157-160; docs/site/tests/e2e/smoke.mjs:38-50].
2. **Given** a description with quoted phrases, **When** the page renders, **Then** up to six of them are listed as "when to use" [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/content.ts:86-90; pages.tsx:162-171; tests/content.test.ts:55].
3. **Given** the page, **When** it renders, **Then** it shows "generated from" with the plugin version and toolkit version, a link to the source SKILL.md at the build's ref, the body as Markdown and the plugin's other skills [OBSERVED: pages.tsx:173-200].
4. **Given** an unknown id, **When** the page opens, **Then** a not-found message with a link back to the index is shown [OBSERVED: pages.tsx:131-144].

---

### User Story 2 - Find a skill by the words of a task (Priority: P1)

A user types task words into the search field (landing or skills page) and gets the matching skills; `/` focuses the field from anywhere outside a text input.

**Why this priority**: the landing page's hero is the search field.

**Independent Test**: `tests/content.test.ts` "finds a skill by the words of a task" / "by its Claude Code command" / "returns nothing for an empty query".

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the query "load test", **When** it is typed, **Then** only skills whose command, id, name, plugin or description contain every term are listed, ranked by id [OBSERVED: docs/site/src/content.ts:66-83].

# Feature Specification: LLM-readable output

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `docs/site/scripts/generate-llms.ts`, run as the last step of `bun run build`.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - An agent maps the toolkit from llms.txt (Priority: P1)

An agent fetching over HTTP, without JavaScript, reads `llms.txt`, follows a link to a page's `.md` and answers a toolkit question from plain Markdown.

**Why this priority**: the brief's journey 3 and architecture driver 4.

**Independent Test**: `bun run build`, then read `dist/llms.txt` and one linked `dist/docs/en-US/skills/<id>.md`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a build, **When** `generate-llms.ts` runs, **Then** `dist/llms.txt` lists a "Use" section (install and every skill), a "Reference" section (flow, contribute, reference) and an "Optional" section (changelog), each linking `<VITE_SITE_URL>/docs/en-US/<slug>.md` with a one-sentence description [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/generate-llms.ts:166-201].
2. **Given** a skill, **When** its Markdown page is written, **Then** it holds the description, both invoke forms, the "generated from" line, the SKILL.md body and the source link [OBSERVED: generate-llms.ts:22-45].
3. **Given** the built `index.html`, **When** a crawler reads it, **Then** `<link rel="alternate" type="text/plain" href=".../llms.txt">` points at the entry file [OBSERVED: docs/site/index.html:13; tests/meta.test.ts:27].

---

### User Story 2 - The whole corpus in one file (Priority: P2)

An agent downloads `llms-full.txt`: every page's Markdown joined by `---` separators.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a build, **When** the script runs, **Then** `dist/llms-full.txt` and `dist/llms-full-en-US.txt` hold every page body in order [OBSERVED: generate-llms.ts:204-229].

---

### User Story 3 - Locale-keyed output (Priority: P3)

Each locale in `LOCALES` gets `llms-<locale>.txt`, `llms-full-<locale>.txt` and `docs/<locale>/…`; the unsuffixed files are en-US.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `LOCALES = ["en-US"]`, **When** the script runs, **Then** `llms-en-US.txt` and `llms.txt` carry the same list [OBSERVED: generate-llms.ts:204-224].

### Edge Cases

- The Markdown reference page lists 6 contracts; the HTML page lists 9 (secrets, agent roles and tracker sync are missing) [OBSERVED: generate-llms.ts:148-153 vs docs/site/src/pages.tsx:304-345].
- The Markdown install page omits the HTML page's Verify, Updates and first-skill sections; the Markdown contribute page omits Layout and the versions table [OBSERVED: generate-llms.ts:54-137 vs pages.tsx:206-299].
- A skill's one-line description is the text before the first `. `; descriptions with no period are used whole [OBSERVED: generate-llms.ts:27].
- Nothing tests the LLM output: no unit test reads `dist/llms*.txt` and CI only asserts the Open Graph files [OBSERVED: docs/site/tests/; .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml:67-84].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The build MUST emit `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and one `.md` per page and locale from the same content the pages render.
- **FR-002**: `.md`, `llms*.txt` MUST be served `no-cache` with `text/markdown` / `text/plain` (feature 005) [OBSERVED: .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml:250-263].
- **FR-003**: Links in `llms.txt` MUST be absolute, from `VITE_SITE_URL`.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Every page reachable in the HTML site has a Markdown twin with the same sections. *Not met today* (see Edge Cases).

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: the Markdown twins are meant to carry the same content as the HTML pages; the gaps above are drift, not intent.]

# Feature Specification: Docs site build, checks and R2 deploy

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `.github/workflows/docs-ci.yml`, `docs/site/tests/e2e/smoke.mjs` and `docs/site/scripts/og-image.ts`.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Every docs change is verified (Priority: P1)

On a push to `main` or `dev` or a pull request touching `docs/site/**` or `docs/product/**`, CI installs with the frozen lockfile, lints, typechecks, unit-tests and builds the site under the repository-name prefix, and asserts the build.

**Why this priority**: the only gate between a change and the public site.

**Independent Test**: the `verify` job of a Docs CI run.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a change under the trigger paths, **When** Docs CI runs, **Then** `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` and `build` run in order [OBSERVED: .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml:3-66].
2. **Given** a build, **When** it finishes, **Then** CI fails unless `index.html` loads assets from `/<repo>/assets/` [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:67-76].
3. **Given** a build, **When** it finishes, **Then** CI fails unless `dist/og-image.png` exists and `og:image` and `twitter:image` are advertised [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:78-84].
4. **Given** the workflow file, **When** CI runs, **Then** any `aws s3 sync|cp` line not using `$R2_PREFIX` fails the build [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:86-95].

---

### User Story 2 - The built site works in a real browser (Priority: P1)

CI serves the built site and drives it with containerized Chrome (selenium/standalone-chrome, pinned by digest): landing, flow page, a skill page and the not-found route.

**Independent Test**: `bun run build`, `vite preview`, `SELENIUM_URL=… bun run e2e`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the e2e job, **When** it runs, **Then** Chrome is started by digest with `--network host` and the smoke asserts four pages [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:105-170; docs/site/tests/e2e/smoke.mjs:19-61].
2. **Given** the last Docs CI runs on `main` and `dev` (2026-10-17), **When** checked, **Then** they succeeded [OBSERVED: `gh run list --workflow docs-ci.yml` → run 39067000179 success].

---

### User Story 3 - Publish after a release (Priority: P1)

After `release.yml` completes successfully on `main`, the deploy job rebuilds `main` (so the footer shows the new tag) and syncs it to Cloudflare R2 under `/<repo>/`, with immutable caching for hashed assets and `no-cache` for entry, LLM and Markdown files.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a successful `release` workflow_run, **When** deploy runs, **Then** it builds with `VITE_BASE_PATH=/<repo>/` in environment `ai-gent-docs` [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:172-207].
2. **Given** R2 credentials are absent, **When** deploy runs, **Then** it warns and skips every sync step, and the job succeeds [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:210-218].
3. **Given** credentials, **When** deploy runs, **Then** it validates the endpoint (`https://`), bucket and prefix shape (`/<slug>/`) before syncing [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:220-226].
4. **Given** the sync, **When** it runs, **Then** `assets/` is synced with `--delete` and `max-age=31536000, immutable`, `index.html` and `llms*.txt` with `no-cache`, and `docs/` as `text/markdown` with `--delete`, all under `$R2_PREFIX` [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:231-263].

---

### User Story 4 - Regenerate the preview image (Priority: P3)

A maintainer runs `bun run og` to rebuild the committed `public/og-image.png` (1200×630) from `scripts/og-image.svg` with sharp.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `scripts/og-image.svg`, **When** `bun run og` runs, **Then** `public/og-image.png` is rewritten [OBSERVED: docs/site/scripts/og-image.ts; docs/site/package.json `og`].

### Edge Cases

- The deploy job does not wait for the `e2e` job; e2e is advisory [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:105-108,172-176].
- Hashed assets are deleted before the new `index.html` is uploaded; a reader holding the old `index.html` during the sync can get 404s for old chunks [INFERRED: sync order docs-ci.yml:231-248 → a short broken window per deploy; confirm by loading the site during a deploy, or upload assets without `--delete` first and prune after].
- Third-party actions in this workflow are referenced by tag (`actions/checkout@v4`, `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`) and Bun by major (`"1"`), while `check.yml` and `release.yml` pin by SHA [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:36,40,98,112,114,195,199 vs .github/workflows/check.yml:22].
- A missing-credentials deploy is a green run that published nothing [OBSERVED: docs-ci.yml:216].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Every R2 write MUST be scoped to `$R2_PREFIX`; a root-scoped sync MUST fail CI.
- **FR-002**: The prefix MUST derive from the repository name, never from configuration.
- **FR-003**: Deploy MUST run only after a successful release on `main`.
- **FR-004**: CI MUST fail when the base path or the Open Graph image drifts.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Docs CI green on `main` and `dev` [OBSERVED: run 39067000179, 2026-10-17].
- **SC-002**: Zero writes outside `/ai-gent/` in the bucket.

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: the R2 credentials are configured in the `ai-gent-docs` environment; the deploy run's sync output wasn't read.]

# Feature Specification: Installer (install.sh and setup.sh)

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `install.sh` (POSIX sh, 84 lines), `setup.sh` (bash, 862 lines) and `scripts/test-install.sh`.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - One-line install and update (Priority: P1)

A developer runs `curl -fsSL …/install.sh | sh`. The installer clones the toolkit (or updates the existing clone) and runs `setup.sh`, which links every skill and plugin for Claude Code.

**Why this priority**: the toolkit's only install path.

**Independent Test**: `scripts/test-install.sh` "clones into the default directory", "links point into the clone", "re-run updates in place".

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** no clone, **When** `install.sh` runs, **Then** it clones `AI_GENT_REPO` into `AI_GENT_DIR` (default `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/ai-gent`) and runs `setup.sh` with the same arguments [OBSERVED: install.sh:41-79; scripts/test-install.sh:231-233].
2. **Given** a clean clone on a branch, **When** it runs again, **Then** it fast-forwards and reports `updated A → B` or `already at A` [OBSERVED: install.sh:53-64; test-install.sh:235].
3. **Given** local changes in the clone, **When** it runs, **Then** it doesn't update and links what's there [OBSERVED: install.sh:47-48; test-install.sh:238].
4. **Given** `AI_GENT_DIR` exists and isn't a clone, **When** it runs, **Then** it stops with an error [OBSERVED: install.sh:66-67; test-install.sh:240].
5. **Given** a partial download, **When** `sh` runs it, **Then** nothing executes, because all work is in `main()` called on the last line [OBSERVED: install.sh:16-17,84].

---

### User Story 2 - Pin a release (Priority: P2)

A user sets `AI_GENT_BRANCH=<tag>` to pin the clone; later runs keep the pin until a new value moves it.

**Independent Test**: `test-install.sh` "clones at the tag", "stays pinned without AI_GENT_BRANCH", "moves the pin to a newer tag".

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `AI_GENT_BRANCH=9.9.0`, **When** installing fresh, **Then** the clone is at that tag [OBSERVED: install.sh:71-72; test-install.sh:254].
2. **Given** a detached (pinned) clone and no `AI_GENT_BRANCH`, **When** it runs, **Then** it stays pinned and says so [OBSERVED: install.sh:51-52; test-install.sh:256].
3. **Given** a pinned clone and a newer tag in `AI_GENT_BRANCH`, **When** it runs, **Then** it fetches and checks out that tag detached [OBSERVED: install.sh:26-31; test-install.sh:258].

---

### User Story 3 - Install for other agents (Priority: P1)

A user picks agents with `--target` (or in the selector): opencode gets symlinks, generated entry files and `/<plugin>-<skill>` commands; Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Amp share generated entries in `~/.agents/skills`; Kiro, Windsurf and Antigravity each get their own.

**Independent Test**: `test-install.sh` lines 60-126.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `--target claude`, **When** setup runs, **Then** each `skills/<n>/` and `plugins/<n>/` is symlinked into `CLAUDE_SKILLS_DIR` [OBSERVED: setup.sh:365-381; test-install.sh:63].
2. **Given** opencode is chosen, **When** setup runs, **Then** each plugin skill gets a generated `<plugin>-<skill>/SKILL.md` pointing at its source and a command file; forked skills (`context: fork`) become `subtask: true` commands [OBSERVED: setup.sh:389-473,621-678; test-install.sh:64-72].
3. **Given** several shared-directory agents, **When** setup runs, **Then** one pass writes one entry per skill into `AGENTS_SKILLS_DIR`, as files not symlinks [OBSERVED: setup.sh:84,834-856; test-install.sh:119-121].
4. **Given** non-Claude, non-opencode agents, **When** setup finishes, **Then** it notes that the guards are instructions only there [OBSERVED: setup.sh:706; test-install.sh:124].
5. **Given** `--target nope`, **When** setup runs, **Then** it exits 2 [OBSERVED: setup.sh:141-146; test-install.sh:132].
6. **Given** a choice was made, **When** setup runs later with `--skip-prompt` or without a terminal, **Then** the remembered choice is used (first time: Claude Code, plus opencode if an earlier run generated its entries) [OBSERVED: setup.sh:725-734,817-832; test-install.sh:126-151].

---

### User Story 4 - Safe, idempotent re-runs and uninstall (Priority: P1)

Re-running changes nothing that is already right, removes links and entries whose source is gone, never overwrites what it didn't create without `--force` (which backs it up), and `--uninstall` removes only what it installed.

**Independent Test**: `test-install.sh` lines 58-113, 153-162.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an installed toolkit, **When** setup re-runs, **Then** nothing is linked or generated [OBSERVED: test-install.sh:81].
2. **Given** `--dry-run`, **When** setup runs, **Then** nothing changes [OBSERVED: setup.sh:148-156; test-install.sh:58].
3. **Given** a real directory where a link should go, **When** setup runs without `--force`, **Then** it is kept and the skip reported; with `--force` it is moved to `<name>.bak-<timestamp>` and linked [OBSERVED: setup.sh:310-340; test-install.sh:110-113].
4. **Given** a generated entry directory without the `.ai-gent-generated` marker, **When** setup runs, **Then** it is left alone [OBSERVED: setup.sh:399].
5. **Given** `--uninstall`, **When** setup runs, **Then** links into the repo, generated entries and commands are removed, the user's own files are kept and the remembered choice is forgotten [OBSERVED: setup.sh:343-352,474-488; test-install.sh:155-162].

---

### User Story 5 - opencode guard configuration (Priority: P2)

With opencode chosen, setup offers ([Y/n]) to merge the OpenCode V2 permission rules mirroring the guard hooks, the guard plugin and `skill` denies for the short colliding IDs into `opencode.json`; `--yes` applies, `--no-config-edits`, `--dry-run` or no terminal print the snippet instead; uninstall removes only what it added.

**Independent Test**: `test-install.sh` lines 164-226.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** no terminal and no `--yes`, **When** setup runs, **Then** `opencode.json` is untouched and the rules are printed [OBSERVED: setup.sh:506-518; test-install.sh:184-186].
2. **Given** the user's conflicting rule, **When** merging, **Then** the user's rule is kept and the conflict reported; missing rules are appended after the user's and a backup is kept [OBSERVED: test-install.sh:192-199].
3. **Given** a config with comments, **When** setup runs, **Then** the file is left alone and the snippet printed [OBSERVED: test-install.sh:214-215].

---

### User Story 6 - Choose agents interactively (Priority: P3)

On a terminal, setup shows an fzf selector (a numbered prompt without fzf) with Claude Code and the previous choice preselected and a "found" column per agent.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a terminal, **When** setup runs without `--target`/`--skip-prompt`, **Then** the selector opens; choosing nothing exits 1 with "no agent chosen" [OBSERVED: setup.sh:740-810]. **No test** (needs a TTY).

### Edge Cases

- `setup.sh` requires bash with associative arrays (`declare -A`, bash ≥ 4) [OBSERVED: setup.sh:71]; `install.sh` checks only that `bash` exists [OBSERVED: install.sh:39] [INFERRED: macOS's stock bash 3.2 would fail at line 71; confirm on macOS — the README's supported platforms weren't checked].
- `--target` as the last argument with no value: `shift` past the end under `set -e` ends the script silently [INFERRED: setup.sh:127,139 → exit without a message; confirm with `setup.sh --target`].
- `--uninstall --target codex` prunes the whole shared `~/.agents/skills` entry set, so Cursor, Copilot and Amp lose their entries too [INFERRED: setup.sh:680-689 prunes the directory, not per agent; confirm whether that is intended].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The installer MUST never execute a partially downloaded script.
- **FR-002**: Setup MUST be idempotent and MUST NOT replace anything it didn't create unless `--force`, which backs it up.
- **FR-003**: Each agent's directory MUST be overridable by its environment variable (`CLAUDE_SKILLS_DIR`, `OPENCODE_SKILLS_DIR`, `OPENCODE_COMMANDS_DIR`, `AGENTS_SKILLS_DIR`, `KIRO_SKILLS_DIR`, `WINDSURF_SKILLS_DIR`) [OBSERVED: setup.sh:48-53].
- **FR-004**: The agent choice MUST persist in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/ai-gent/targets`.
- **FR-005**: opencode config edits MUST be asked, reversible and never touch a file with comments.

### Key Entities

- **Agent**, **Generated entry**, **Targets state**, **Config record** — see `data-model.md`.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `scripts/test-install.sh` (70 checks) passes in CI [OBSERVED: release run 39066868067 on 0d34208 ran `check.yml`, which runs it, and succeeded].

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: Linux is the supported platform; the shared-directory prune on uninstall is intended.]

# Feature Specification: Secrets through pass (passstore)

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `shared/passstore.py` (72 lines), symlinked as `plugins/db/scripts/passstore.py` and `plugins/repo/scripts/passstore.py`, and the contract `shared/secrets.md`.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - A runner reads a credential without exposing it (Priority: P1)

`dbrun` or `reporun` needs a password or token: it checks that the entry exists without decrypting, then reads it through `pass show` only for the call that needs it; the value never reaches output.

**Why this priority**: the credential contract (`shared/secrets.md`) for every runner.

**Independent Test**: dbrun's `test_sources_in_order`, `test_bad_or_unreadable_entry`; reporun's `test_detect_never_decrypts`, `test_missing_entry` (fake `pass` on PATH, temporary `PASSWORD_STORE_DIR`).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** entry `ai-gent/db/app`, **When** `has()` is called, **Then** it checks `<store>/ai-gent/db/app.gpg` exists and decrypts nothing [OBSERVED: shared/passstore.py:38-40].
2. **Given** an existing entry, **When** `read()` is called, **Then** `pass show` runs with stdin closed and a 90 s timeout; the first line is the secret, the rest are notes [OBSERVED: passstore.py:43-59].
3. **Given** a locked store or empty entry, **When** `read()` is called, **Then** `StoreError` says how to unlock it in the user's own terminal, never including a value [OBSERVED: passstore.py:55-58].
4. **Given** a name with a leading `-` or `/`, or a `..` segment, **When** any call is made, **Then** it is refused [OBSERVED: passstore.py:17,32-35].

---

### User Story 2 - Move a plain-text secret into pass (Priority: P2)

`dbrun secrets migrate` writes a value as a new entry with `pass insert --multiline`; it never overwrites an existing entry.

**Independent Test**: dbrun `test_migrate`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an absent entry, **When** `write()` is called, **Then** `pass insert --multiline` receives the value on stdin and the entry must exist afterwards [OBSERVED: passstore.py:62-72].
2. **Given** an existing entry, **When** `write()` is called, **Then** `StoreError("… already exists")` [OBSERVED: passstore.py:67-68].

### Edge Cases

- The prefix is `AI_GENT_PASS_PREFIX` (default `ai-gent`); the store is `PASSWORD_STORE_DIR` (default `~/.password-store`) [OBSERVED: passstore.py:24-29; dbrun test_prefix_override].
- `has()` checks only the file; a store with a `.gpg-id` for a missing key passes `has()` and fails `read()` [INFERRED: passstore.py:40 → existence ≠ readability; the runners report the `read()` error].
- The insert failure message carries the last 300 characters of `pass`'s stderr [OBSERVED: passstore.py:72] [INFERRED: pass doesn't echo the value on stderr, so no leak; confirm with a failing gpg].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Values MUST only be returned to the caller, never printed or put in a message.
- **FR-002**: Entry names MUST match `ENTRY_RE` and contain no `..` segment.
- **FR-003**: Writes MUST NOT overwrite.
- **FR-004**: The module MUST be imported only on the host, never inside a runner's client container [OBSERVED: passstore.py:2-3; plugins/db/scripts/dbrun.py:288-292].

### Key Entities

- **Entry** — `<prefix>/<area>/<name>` (`ai-gent/db/<profile>`, `ai-gent/github/pat`, …); first line secret, other lines notes (`email:`, `username:`…) used by reporun [OBSERVED: plugins/repo/scripts/reporun.py:119-138].

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: No test output contains a fake secret value [OBSERVED: reporun test_token_in_env_only_and_redacted; dbrun test_listing_shows_source_never_value].

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: the module has no tests of its own on purpose; it is exercised through the dbrun and reporun suites.]

# Feature Specification: Audited database runner (dbrun)

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `plugins/db/scripts/dbrun.py` (1837 lines), `plugins/db/scripts/test_dbrun.py` and `scripts/test-dbrun-engines.py`. The `db:*` skills' Markdown is out of scope; `plugins/db/references/safety.md` and `runner.md` are the rules this code enforces.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Know which databases exist and what they really are (Priority: P1)

An agent lists connection profiles (from TOML/.env files and running compose containers of this repository) and classifies one: `local` only when proven, otherwise the declared class, defaulting to `production`.

**Why this priority**: every other command's permissions depend on the class.

**Independent Test**: `test_declared_local_without_proof_is_production`, `test_container_or_pod`, `test_listing_never_shows_secrets`, `test_families_and_precedence`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `AI_GENT_DB_CONNECTIONS` or `connections.toml` then `.env` in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/ai-gent/db`, **When** `dbrun profiles` runs, **Then** profiles are listed with engine, class and secret source, never a value [OBSERVED: plugins/db/scripts/dbrun.py:151-161,1181-1201].
2. **Given** a running container started by this repository's compose project with a known engine image, **When** profiles are listed, **Then** it appears as `local:<service>` [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:407-422].
3. **Given** a profile declared `local` whose container isn't proven (no engine, remote `DOCKER_HOST`/`CONTAINER_HOST`, container missing, stopped, a proxy image, or another repository's compose project), **When** classified, **Then** it is `production` and not writable, with the reason as evidence [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:471-526,454-468].
4. **Given** a SQLite file inside this repository and not a symlink, **When** classified, **Then** it is local and writable; outside, read-only [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:477-486].
5. **Given** a name defined twice, **When** profiles load, **Then** dbrun fails with "defined twice" [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:425-431].

---

### User Story 2 - Read safely, anywhere (Priority: P1)

`dbrun query` runs only read-only statements, in a read-only session with statement and lock timeouts, a row cap and masking of personal data, after logging the statements and the reason.

**Why this priority**: the only operation allowed on remote databases.

**Independent Test**: `test_reads`, `test_writes`, `test_backslash_trick_refused`, `test_star_and_counts_on_user_tables`, `test_read_masks_and_logs`, `test_row_cap`, `test_remote_refusals`, `test_remote_read_is_read_only_even_past_the_classifier`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** any statement not starting with a read keyword, or containing a write word, a locking clause, `INTO`, a sequence advance, a side-effect function or an Oracle `DBMS_*`/`UTL_*` package, **When** queried, **Then** it is refused (exit 3) — unknown means write [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:660-693,1250-1254].
2. **Given** a non-local target, **When** a statement uses `SELECT *` or an unfiltered `COUNT(` on a user table, **Then** it is refused unless `--allow-full-count`; catalog queries are exempt [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:713-727].
3. **Given** a read, **When** it runs, **Then** the session is read-only (`default_transaction_read_only`, `SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, SQLite `mode=ro` + `query_only`) with `statement_timeout`/equivalent and a 5 s lock timeout, and is rolled back [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:45,905-978,1022-1068].
4. **Given** columns named like secrets, emails, documents, phones, cards, birth dates, addresses, IPs or names, **When** results print, **Then** values are masked (secrets always, even with `--reveal`) and the masked columns are listed [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:730-836; test_reveal_keeps_secrets_redacted].
5. **Given** more rows than `--max-rows` (default 100), **When** results print, **Then** they are truncated and say so [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1766,1285-1287].
6. **Given** `--explain`, **When** the target is Oracle and remote, **Then** refused (EXPLAIN PLAN writes PLAN_TABLE); elsewhere a plain plan, never `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:676-680,1256-1257].

---

### User Story 3 - Change a proven local database with a backup (Priority: P1)

On a proven local database, `plan` records the statements and expected row counts; after the user confirms, `apply --confirmed` re-proves "local", backs up, runs everything in one transaction and commits only if every expected count matches; `restore --confirmed` puts the backup back.

**Independent Test**: `test_plan_apply_restore`, `test_apply_rolls_back_on_count_mismatch`, `test_tampered_plan_refused`, `test_system_databases_refused_for_writes`; `scripts/test-dbrun-engines.py` against real engines (not run here, not in CI).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a non-writable class, **When** `plan`, `apply` or `restore` runs, **Then** it is refused with the evidence and a pointer to `dbrun script` [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1303-1307].
2. **Given** a system database (`master`, `mysql`, `template1`, …), **When** `plan` or `apply` runs, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1311-1324].
3. **Given** DDL on an engine dbrun can't back up (Oracle), **When** planning, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1310,1335-1338].
4. **Given** a plan, **When** it is recorded, **Then** it is written `0600`, exclusive-create, with a SHA-256 of its statements; `apply` refuses a plan made for another profile or whose statements no longer match the hash [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1339-1352,1371-1382].
5. **Given** `apply` without `--confirmed`, **When** run, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1463-1464].
6. **Given** an expected count mismatch or an error, **When** applying, **Then** the transaction rolls back; on MySQL/MariaDB DDL the output says DDL committed and how to restore [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1052-1060,1482-1487].

---

### User Story 4 - Hand a change to a person for any other database (Priority: P2)

`dbrun script` writes a change script for a person to review and run — transaction wrapper, pre-check, verification and rollback sections — and never executes it.

**Independent Test**: `test_script_never_executes`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an `UPDATE` or `DELETE` without `WHERE`, **When** scripting, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1550-1553].
2. **Given** an existing `--out` file, **When** scripting, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1547-1549].
3. **Given** valid statements, **When** scripting, **Then** the file is written and the log says "not executed"; no password is read [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1541-1589].

---

### User Story 5 - Every action leaves a trail (Priority: P2)

Before a statement runs, an entry is appended to a per-day, per-repository Markdown log (`0600`) with action, profile, class, evidence, reason and statements; the result is appended after. `dbrun log --tail N` shows it.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** any query, plan, apply, restore, script or session action, **When** it starts, **Then** `log_start` writes "status: started" first [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:856-889].
2. **Given** log text, **When** it is written, **Then** known secrets, host, user and password values are redacted [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:838-854,866; test_host_user_password_redacted].

---

### User Story 6 - Credentials stay out of the agent's reach (Priority: P2)

Passwords come from pass first (`pass:` references, then `ai-gent/db/<family>`, then `ai-gent/db/<profile>`), a plain-text file last; `secrets migrate` moves plain-text passwords into pass; `profiles --export-env` writes a `.env` with `pass:` references. Drivers run in a child process that gets credentials only on stdin.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a profile without a password, **When** loaded, **Then** the family entry is tried before the profile entry [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:318-333; test_family_default_entry].
2. **Given** `secrets migrate <profile>` or `--all`, **When** run, **Then** values move into pass and the file lines become references, never shown [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1622-1723; test_migrate].
3. **Given** a remote target, **When** the driver runs, **Then** it's `uv run --with <driver>` on the host; for a local container, a client container joins the database container's network namespace (by `ns:` path inside a podman pod) with the script mounted read-only [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:529-538,1081-1127].

---

### User Story 7 - Warm session for an investigation (Priority: P3)

`dbrun session start|stop|status` keeps a client container running so repeated queries skip the startup.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `session start`, **When** run, **Then** a container `sleep infinity` with the same network and mounts starts and later queries reuse it; `stop` removes it [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1591-1619].

### Edge Cases

- `restore` re-proves "local" but, unlike `apply`, doesn't call `require_user_database` [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1501-1506 vs 1467-1468] — harmless today since a system database can't get a plan, but asymmetric.
- The plan hash lives in the same file as the statements; it catches accidental edits, not a deliberate rewrite of both [INFERRED: dbrun.py:1346,1380 → integrity, not authenticity; the file is `0600` in the user's state dir].
- `script`'s "no WHERE" check looks for the word anywhere in the statement, so a `WHERE` in a subquery satisfies it [INFERRED: dbrun.py:1551-1553; confirm with `DELETE FROM t USING (SELECT … WHERE …) s`].
- The client image defaults to the tag `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm-slim` (no digest) and drivers are unpinned (`psycopg[binary]`, `PyMySQL`, `pymssql`, `oracledb`) [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:36-44].
- A started session container has no lifetime limit [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:1611-1612].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Unknown targets MUST be treated as production; `local` MUST be proven per run.
- **FR-002**: Remote targets MUST only be read, in a read-only session, with timeouts.
- **FR-003**: Writes MUST need a recorded plan, the user's confirmation (`--confirmed`), a fresh local proof and a backup where the engine allows.
- **FR-004**: Results MUST be masked by column name and free-text patterns (email, CPF, CNPJ, Luhn-valid card numbers); secrets MUST stay masked under `--reveal`.
- **FR-005**: Every action MUST be logged before it runs, redacted.
- **FR-006**: Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 refused, 4 connection [OBSERVED: dbrun.py:32].

### Key Entities

See `data-model.md`.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `python3 -m unittest plugins/db/scripts/test_dbrun.py` passes [OBSERVED: `scripts/check.sh --quick` 2026-10-18 → "dbrun (Ran 51 tests)" ok].
- **SC-002**: Zero writes ever reach a non-local target.

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: `scripts/test-dbrun-engines.py` passes against the five server engines; it wasn't run in this reconstruction and isn't in CI.]

# Feature Specification: Platform runner (reporun)

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `plugins/repo/scripts/reporun.py` (765 lines) and `plugins/repo/scripts/test_reporun.py`. The `repo:*` skills' Markdown is out of scope.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Detect the platform and token state (Priority: P1)

An agent runs `reporun detect` and learns the repository's platform (from the remote URL or `git config ai-gent.platform`), its owner/project, whether the platform CLI is installed and signed in, and whether the token entry exists in pass — without decrypting anything.

**Independent Test**: `test_platforms`, `test_forced_platform`, `test_detect_never_decrypts`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps or Bitbucket remote, **When** `detect` runs, **Then** the platform and its coordinates are reported [OBSERVED: plugins/repo/scripts/reporun.py:163-216,238-273].
2. **Given** a Jira URL in `git config ai-gent.jira.url` or a Jira entry, **When** `detect` runs, **Then** Jira is reported too [OBSERVED: reporun.py:243-249].
3. **Given** a missing token, **When** `detect` prints, **Then** it shows the `pass insert -m <entry>` to run in the user's own terminal [OBSERVED: reporun.py:270-271].

---

### User Story 2 - Read through the platform CLI or REST API (Priority: P1)

An agent reads issues, PRs and checks through `reporun cli <platform> -- <args>` (gh, glab, az, jira) or `reporun api <platform> METHOD PATH` with the token from pass, never on a command line and never printed.

**Independent Test**: `test_cli`, `test_api`, `test_github_bearer_and_placeholders`, `test_azure_basic_and_api_version`, `test_jira_basic_with_email`, `test_gitlab_project_path_encoded`, `test_bitbucket_pagination`, `test_token_in_env_only_and_redacted`, `test_errors_redacted`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a CLI call, **When** a token is in pass, **Then** it is passed only in the child's environment (`GH_TOKEN`, `GITLAB_TOKEN`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN`; `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` for GHES), debug variables are dropped, and stderr names the source [OBSERVED: reporun.py:52-58,330-347].
2. **Given** an API call, **When** it runs, **Then** auth is Bearer, or Basic for Azure DevOps (`:token`) and for Bitbucket/Jira with a user note; `{owner}`-style placeholders are filled and URL-encoded; Azure gets `api-version=7.1` [OBSERVED: reporun.py:412-428,483-498].
3. **Given** an absolute URL on another host, **When** called, **Then** refused: "the token goes nowhere else" [OBSERVED: reporun.py:485-487; test_other_hosts_refused].
4. **Given** `--paginate`, **When** called, **Then** pages follow the platform's next link up to `--max-pages` (10) [OBSERVED: reporun.py:450-457,509-540].
5. **Given** any output or error, **When** printed, **Then** the token and its Basic encoding are replaced by `<token>` [OBSERVED: reporun.py:140-145].
6. **Given** GitHub with no pass entry, **When** an API call runs, **Then** it proceeds unauthenticated ("none (public)") [OBSERVED: reporun.py:477-481,505-506].

---

### User Story 3 - Writes only when asked (Priority: P1)

Any call that changes something on the platform needs `--write`, which the repo guard turns into a question for the user; CLI subcommands and flags that can print a token or change the CLI's login are refused outright.

**Independent Test**: `test_write_needs_flag`, `test_refusals`, `test_write_with_flag`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a non-GET/HEAD API call (except read-only POSTs: GitHub/GitLab GraphQL without `mutation`, Azure WIQL, Jira search), **When** run without `--write`, **Then** refused, exit 3 [OBSERVED: reporun.py:75-81,430-436,473-475].
2. **Given** a CLI call, **When** no read verb (`list`, `view`, `status`, `checks`, `diff`, …) is among its first four positional words, or an option precedes the subcommand, **Then** it is a write [OBSERVED: reporun.py:61-64,278-309].
3. **Given** `gh auth|alias|extension|secret|codespace|config`, `glab auth|alias|config|variable|token`, `az login|logout|account|extension|config` or `jira init`, or `--debug`/`--show-token`, **When** run, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: reporun.py:66-72,321-325].

---

### User Story 4 - Several calls, one confirmation (Priority: P2)

`reporun batch FILE` runs a JSON plan of named steps in order, with `{{step.field}}` references between them, one `--write` for the whole batch, `--dry-run` to list without calling, and stops at the first failure.

**Independent Test**: `test_needs_write_once`, `test_dry_run_calls_nothing`, `test_references_and_records`, `test_stops_at_first_failure`, `test_reads_need_no_write`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a batch with write steps, **When** run without `--write` or `--dry-run`, **Then** refused, naming up to eight write steps [OBSERVED: reporun.py:604-618].
2. **Given** `--dry-run`, **When** run, **Then** each step prints as read/write and nothing is called [OBSERVED: reporun.py:619-623].
3. **Given** a failing step, **When** run, **Then** later steps don't run and the report is `ok: false`, exit 1 [OBSERVED: reporun.py:625-660].

---

### User Story 5 - The branch chain (Priority: P2)

`reporun chain` derives work → integration (`dev`/`develop`) → [staging (`staging`/`homolog`/`hml`)] → production (`main`/`master`, else the remote default), where stories count as integrated and where closing keywords act, and flags ambiguity to ask about.

**Independent Test**: `test_full_chain`, `test_ambiguous_asks`, `test_no_integration_branch`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** both `dev` and `develop`, **When** `chain` runs, **Then** integration is unset and an ASK line is printed [OBSERVED: reporun.py:665-701].
2. **Given** no integration branch, **When** `chain` runs, **Then** `integrated_on` is production [OBSERVED: reporun.py:689].

### Edge Cases

- A write CLI call whose positional arguments include a read verb is classified as a read and runs without `--write`: `cli_is_write("gh", ["label", "create", "status"])` and `["issue", "edit", "12", "view"]` return `False` [OBSERVED: run `python3 -I -c 'import reporun; …'` in plugins/repo/scripts on 2026-10-18; cause reporun.py:309]. Risk: a platform change without the user's question.
- GraphQL "read" is decided by the absence of the substring `mutation` in the body [OBSERVED: reporun.py:435] — safe for writes (they need the keyword), but a query mentioning "mutation" in a string needs `--write`.
- Redaction skips secrets shorter than 4 characters [OBSERVED: reporun.py:142].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Tokens MUST come from pass entries under `<prefix>/<platform>/`; an entry under `db/` is refused [OBSERVED: reporun.py:100-108].
- **FR-002**: A token MUST NOT appear on a command line, in output or in errors.
- **FR-003**: Writes MUST need `--write` per call or per batch; unknown is a write.
- **FR-004**: A token MUST only be sent to the platform's API host.
- **FR-005**: Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 refused [OBSERVED: reporun.py:36].

### Key Entities

See `data-model.md`.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `test_reporun.py` passes [OBSERVED: `scripts/check.sh --quick` 2026-10-18 → "reporun, specsync (Ran 35 tests)" ok].
- **SC-002**: No platform write without `--write` — *not met* for CLI calls with read-verb arguments (Edge Cases).

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: the repo guard hook (`plugins/repo/hooks/guard.sh`, not reconstructed) is the only thing that asks the user; it keys on `--write`, so the misclassification above bypasses the question.]

# Feature Specification: Specs-to-tracker planner (specsync)

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `plugins/repo/scripts/specsync.py` (438 lines) and `plugins/repo/scripts/test_specsync.py`.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Plan a feature's tracker items (Priority: P1)

`specsync plan <NNN>` reads `specs/NNN-*/spec.md`, `tasks.md`, the feature's row in `specs/README.md` and its `tracker.md`, and prints one item per feature and one per user story — title, body with a hidden marker, tasks as a checklist, target state — and what to do with each (create, update, state, none).

**Why this priority**: what `repo:sync` applies through `reporun batch`.

**Independent Test**: `test_items_and_story_assignment`, `test_states`, `test_all_tasks_checked_is_review`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `### User Story N - Title (Priority: Pn)` headings, **When** planned, **Then** each becomes a story item `[NNN] USn: Title` [OBSERVED: plugins/repo/scripts/specsync.py:37,63-85,334-342].
2. **Given** no such headings but a `## Stories` numbered list (`1. **Title**: …`), **When** planned, **Then** the list's entries are the stories (introspec's shape) [OBSERVED: specsync.py:88-113; test_introspec_story_list].
3. **Given** tasks tagged `[USn]` or under a "User Story n" phase heading, **When** planned, **Then** they go to that story's checklist; others to the feature body [OBSERVED: specsync.py:116-138,309-322].
4. **Given** README statuses, **When** the feature state is computed, **Then** Planned → todo, In progress/Partial → doing, Implemented → review, Verified → done, the least advanced side wins; without statuses, from the tasks [OBSERVED: specsync.py:32-34,166-192; test_status_with_notes_after_it].
5. **Given** a story, **When** its state is computed, **Then** done if the feature is done, else from its tasks (todo / doing / review) [OBSERVED: specsync.py:328].
6. **Given** a tracker item whose title+body hash or state changed, **When** planned, **Then** its action is `update`, `state` or `update+state` [OBSERVED: specsync.py:285-286,344-354].

---

### User Story 2 - Record what the tracker created (Priority: P1)

`specsync record <NNN> --platform P --from batch-output.json` merges a batch's records (key, ref, id, state, hash, url) into the feature's `tracker.md`.

**Independent Test**: `test_tracker_round_trip_and_actions`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** records, **When** recorded, **Then** `tracker.md` is rewritten with platform, last-sync date and a `| Key | Item | Id | State | Hash | URL |` table, feature first then stories by number [OBSERVED: specsync.py:212-227,377-394].

---

### User Story 3 - Every feature at a glance (Priority: P2)

`specsync features` lists every `specs/NNN-*` directory with its state, whether it's synced, and how many items are pending.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `specs/`, **When** `features` runs, **Then** one row per feature with state (or `retired`), synced/not synced and pending count [OBSERVED: specsync.py:397-410].

---

### User Story 4 - Retired features and orphans (Priority: P3)

A feature whose README statuses are all retired words (retired, superseded, removed, dropped, cancelled) plans no items; items in `tracker.md` that no longer match a story are reported as orphans, never deleted.

**Independent Test**: `test_retired_from_notes`, `test_orphans_reported`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a retired feature, **When** planned, **Then** no items, and the output says so [OBSERVED: specsync.py:163,299-301,355-356,360-361].
2. **Given** an orphan, **When** planned, **Then** "orphan … report it; never delete the item" [OBSERVED: specsync.py:357,371-372].

### Edge Cases

- `specs/` is resolved from the current directory, so specsync must run at the repository root [OBSERVED: specsync.py:46-47].
- Story bodies over 6000 characters are cut at a line with `…` [OBSERVED: specsync.py:329].
- README rows match on the first cell's number with leading zeros stripped [OBSERVED: specsync.py:157].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: specsync MUST never call the tracker; it only plans and records.
- **FR-002**: Item state MUST follow the repository (tasks, README), never the tracker.
- **FR-003**: Each item body MUST carry the marker `<!-- ai-gent:sync <path> <key> -->` [OBSERVED: specsync.py:35].

### Key Entities

See `data-model.md`.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `test_specsync.py` passes [OBSERVED: `scripts/check.sh --quick` 2026-10-18, within "Ran 35 tests" ok].
- **SC-002**: `specsync features` parses the reconstructed `specs/` of this repository [OBSERVED: see `docs/product/introspec.md` § Runs].

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: `repo:sync` is the only caller.]

# Feature Specification: Worktrees for parallel tracks (wt.py)

**Feature Branch**: `docs/introspec-site-runners` (reconstructed; the code already exists on `main`)

**Created**: 2026-10-18

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: Reverse-engineered from `plugins/agents/scripts/wt.py` (241 lines) and `plugins/agents/scripts/test_wt.py`.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - See which features can start in parallel (Priority: P1)

`wt.py plan` reads `specs/README.md` and lists features with a side still below Implemented whose dependencies are all Implemented, the ones waiting and on what, and how many are done.

**Independent Test**: `test_plan`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** README rows with a 3-digit first cell, a `Depends on` column and side columns (`frontend`, `backend`, `status`, `qa`), **When** `plan` runs, **Then** each row is ready, blocked or done [OBSERVED: plugins/agents/scripts/wt.py:87-147].
2. **Given** a side marked N/A or —, **When** planned, **Then** it isn't a side to build [OBSERVED: wt.py:110-115].
3. **Given** no `specs/README.md`, **When** `plan` runs, **Then** it fails with "name the tracks yourself" [OBSERVED: wt.py:89-90].

---

### User Story 2 - Start a track in its own worktree (Priority: P1)

`wt.py add <branch>` creates a new branch off the chain's dev branch in `.worktrees/<slug>/`, excluded from git locally, and prints a compose project name and a port offset for that track.

**Independent Test**: `test_add_list_remove`, `test_from_inside_a_worktree`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** exactly one of `dev`/`develop` (local or origin), **When** `add` runs without `--base`, **Then** it is the base; with both or neither it fails asking for `--base` [OBSERVED: wt.py:52-58,150-152].
2. **Given** an existing branch or path, **When** `add` runs, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: wt.py:154-157].
3. **Given** a new track, **When** added, **Then** `/.worktrees/` and `compose.worktree.yaml` are appended to `.git/info/exclude` (no project file changes) [OBSERVED: wt.py:61-68].
4. **Given** the n-th worktree, **When** added, **Then** `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=<repo>-<branch>` and port offset `n × 100` are printed [OBSERVED: wt.py:159-166].
5. **Given** it runs inside a worktree, **When** any command runs, **Then** the main checkout is used as root [OBSERVED: wt.py:42-45].

---

### User Story 3 - List and remove tracks (Priority: P2)

`wt.py list` shows each worktree under `.worktrees/` with ahead/behind against dev and whether it's dirty; `wt.py remove <branch>` removes a clean, fully landed worktree and deletes its branch.

**Independent Test**: `test_add_list_remove`, `test_refusals`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** uncommitted changes, **When** `remove` runs, **Then** refused [OBSERVED: wt.py:204-205].
2. **Given** commits not on dev, **When** `remove` runs, **Then** refused: "land it first" [OBSERVED: wt.py:207-208].
3. **Given** a clean, landed track, **When** `remove` runs, **Then** worktree removed, branch deleted with `-d`, worktrees pruned [OBSERVED: wt.py:209-213].

### Edge Cases

- The port offset is the count of current worktrees + 1, so after a removal a new track can reuse a live track's offset (3 tracks, remove the 1st, add → offset 300 twice) [INFERRED: wt.py:158 → port collisions between parallel stacks; confirm with add ×3, remove first, add].
- `plan` reads `specs/README.md` from the main checkout, not from the worktree it runs in: run from this branch's worktree (which has the README), it failed with "no specs/README.md" because the main checkout has none [OBSERVED: `python3 -I plugins/agents/scripts/wt.py plan` on 2026-10-18; cause wt.py:42-45,88]. Specs that exist only on a branch are invisible to it.
- Only worktrees under `.worktrees/` are listed; agent worktrees elsewhere (such as `.claude/worktrees/`) are invisible to `list` and `remove` [OBSERVED: wt.py:71-82].

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: A track MUST start on a new branch; existing branches are refused.
- **FR-002**: wt.py MUST NOT change tracked project files.
- **FR-003**: `remove` MUST refuse dirty or unlanded tracks.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

# Feature Specification: Checkpoint holds in the session (project mod)

**Feature Branch**: `feat/checkpoint-band`

**Created**: 2026-10-28

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: "Project and implement #1": the first Claude Code mod in ai-gent. It surfaces and enforces the holds `project:checkpoint` records, because today they are only text the next agent has to remember.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - See the holds in force (Priority: P1)

While `.ai-gent/checkpoint.md` lists holds, a band above the prompt shows them, so neither the user nor the agent loses track of a decision in force.

**Independent Test**: `the band lists the holds, on every surface`, `the band stays quiet without holds`, `the band stays quiet without a checkpoint` (`plugins/project/hooks/checkpoint.test.tsx`).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a checkpoint whose `## Holds` has top-level bullets, **When** the session starts or a turn completes, **Then** the band shows `Holds`, the file and its `Updated` time, and up to three holds, with `+N more` for any others.
2. **Given** no checkpoint, an empty `## Holds` or only `- none`, **When** the prompt is drawn, **Then** no band is drawn.
3. **Given** a commit newer than the file, **When** the band is drawn, **Then** it says the file is older than the last commit (the warning `checkpoint.py show` gives).
4. **Given** the user presses Hide, **When** the prompt is drawn again, **Then** the band stays hidden for the rest of the session.

---

### User Story 2 - Ask before a step a hold may cover (Priority: P1)

A go-ahead never carries over from an earlier session (`project:recap`). While any hold is listed, a push, merge, tag or release asks the user first, naming the holds.

**Independent Test**: `a push under a hold asks, and Stop refuses it`, `a push under a hold runs once the person says so`, `without holds, or for a read-only command, nothing is asked`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** holds, **When** the agent runs `git push`, `git merge`, `git tag <name>` (or `-a`/`-s`/`-f`/`-d`), `gh pr merge` or `gh release create`, in any segment of a compound command, **Then** the user is asked whether to stop or run it, and the question lists the holds.
2. **Given** the answer Stop, a dismissed dialog, or a run with nobody to ask, **When** the gate answers, **Then** the command is refused, and the agent reads that holds are in force and that it should ask the user.
3. **Given** no holds, or a read-only command (`git tag`, `git tag -l`, `git merge --abort`, `gh pr list`), **When** it runs, **Then** nothing is asked.

---

### User Story 3 - Turn either part off (Priority: P3)

`holdsBand` and `holdsGate` are `userConfig` booleans (default true), shown in `/config`.

**Independent Test**: `the gate can be turned off`.

### Edge Cases

- The session runs in a subdirectory: the file is looked up at the git top level, as `checkpoint.py` does. Outside git, it is looked up in the session's directory.
- The file is rewritten during a turn: the gate re-reads it before asking, so a hold lifted mid-turn no longer asks.
- A hook reload resets the module's variables. The parsed checkpoint lives in `$.state` with a shape tag, so a reload keeps the band.
- The gate fails (git missing, unreadable file): it lets the command through. The `git` guard still asks on every push.
- The `git` guard also asks before a push, so a push under a hold asks twice. This is deliberate: the two questions are about different things.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

- **FR-001**: The mod reads `.ai-gent/checkpoint.md` only. It never writes it; `checkpoint.py` and the skill stay its only writers.
- **FR-002**: Holds and rules are the top-level `- `/`* ` bullets of `## Holds` and `## Rules in force`. Indented lines continue the bullet above, and HTML comments and empty markers (`none`, `n/a`, `—`) are ignored.
- **FR-003**: The mod is Claude Code-only and optional. Nothing in `shared/pipeline.md`, `project:checkpoint` or `project:recap` depends on it.
- **FR-004**: It lives in the plugin it serves: `plugins/project/hooks/register.tsx`, named under `modules` in `hooks/hooks.json`, with its state contract in `plugins/project/types/index.d.ts`. It installs through the existing `setup.sh` link.

## Success Criteria

- **SC-001**: `claude plugin validate plugins/project` and `claude plugin test plugins/project` pass in `scripts/check.sh` and in CI.
- **SC-002**: In a live session with a hold in the checkpoint, the band shows the hold, and `git push` asks before the `git` guard's own question.

## Out of scope

Writing the checkpoint, matching a hold's text to a particular command (every listed hold gates every gated command), and opencode or the other agents.

## Conventions this feature settles for later mods (013–017)

The mod's folder is its owning plugin. `scripts/check.sh` runs `claude plugin test` for every plugin whose `hooks.json` names `modules`. CI pins Claude Code to 2.1.312 or later. `.gitignore` ignores `plugins/*/.claude-plugin/types/`. Opt-outs are `userConfig` booleans. Functions that take `$` are declared at the module's top level, as the validator requires. A pure helper (`hooks/checkpoint.ts`) carries the parsing so it can be unit-tested.
