# Feature Specification: Container and disk band

**Feature Branch**: `docs/mod-specs-2` (specification only; built on its own branch)

**Created**: 2026-10-31

**Status**: Implemented

**Input**: A Claude Code mod that keeps this project's container leftovers and a low disk in view all session, not only as the toast at its start: a band above the prompt fed by what `plugins/devcontainer/hooks/leftovers.sh` already reports, now also as JSON (`leftovers.sh --json`, a separate change landed first): a disk under the floor, dangling images of this project, volumes of worktrees that are gone, buildah working containers in the store; refreshed after container work, plus `/containers` printing the full report. Report only: nothing here removes anything.

**Depends on**: 017 (repo hygiene) — the `devcontainer` module, its `leftovers.sh` relay and `hook-lines.ts`; the prerequisite change `leftovers.sh --json` (below); 011 (worktrees) — `wt.py resources`, which names the commands the report points at; 012 (checkpoint mod) — layout, `check.sh` wiring, versioning and install.

## Context and ground rules

- **What exists.** `leftovers.sh` is the plugin's `SessionStart` hook (`plugins/devcontainer/hooks/hooks.json`). It reads the engine (`CONTAINER_ENGINE`, else podman, else docker), computes the project label `me.lucasvmigotto.ai-gent.project=<project>` from the repository's name, and prints `ai-gent containers (report only, nothing removed):` followed by up to four lines: `disk: N GB free on the container store (<path>), under the F GB floor; …`, `N dangling image(s) of <project>: …`, `N volume(s) of <project> belong to worktrees that are gone: …`, `N buildah working container(s) in the store (interrupted builds, any project): …`. It is silent when there is nothing to say, no engine, or not a git checkout, and `AI_GENT_NO_LEFTOVERS_CHECK=1` disables it. Spec 017 made the report a toast, once per session (`plugins/devcontainer/hooks/leftovers.ts`). The order of its lines, which the band keeps: disk, dangling images, volumes, buildah.
- **Prerequisite change (Planned, lands before this mod): `leftovers.sh --json`.** Default output is untouched (the SessionStart hook and 017's toast keep reading the same text, silent when clean). With `--json` the script always prints one JSON object when it ran: `{"checked": true, "project": "shop", "findings": [{"kind": "disk", "free_gb": 14, "floor_gb": 20, "store": "/path"}, {"kind": "dangling", "count": 2}, {"kind": "volumes", "count": 1}, {"kind": "buildah", "count": 21}]}` (an empty `findings` array when clean), and `{"checked": false, "reason": "no-engine" | "not-a-checkout" | "disabled"}` when it could not check, so the mod never mistakes "couldn't check" for "clean". `scripts/test-containers-guard.sh` gains `--json` cases (findings, clean, disabled by `AI_GENT_NO_LEFTOVERS_CHECK=1`, a fake engine), and `scripts/consistency.py` pins the key names the mod reads. The JSON carries counts and numbers only, never the advice sentences (the mod's pointer text is its own, FR-002).
- **Supersedes 017's FR-005 for this plugin.** 017 FR-005 says the `SessionStart` scripts "MUST NOT be run a second time" (its toast reads the stored hook row instead). This feature runs `leftovers.sh --json` again, on purpose: the band must refresh after container work, which no stored row can give. The session-start toast keeps its single read of the stored row; the band's reads are separate, throttled and JSON.
- **The rule it serves.** `shared/containers.md` §9a: resources are labelled with the project's label and removed **by ID or by label**, never by a prune; what isn't the project's own is listed with sizes and **asked**; the disk floor is 20 GB or 10 % of the disk, whichever is larger; "report what's left" ends every handoff that ran containers. The band makes §9a's last bullet continuous instead of a one-off.
- **Same stance as 017.** The mod relays the script's own findings and computes no check of its own; it never removes, stops or builds anything, and what it names to run is only what the script already names (`wt.py finish`, `wt.py resources`, the project's `clean` recipe), all by-ID or by-label.
- Owner: the `devcontainer` plugin; its module `plugins/devcontainer/hooks/register.tsx` (shared with 015's and 017's parts).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Leftovers stay visible (Priority: P1)

Once `leftovers.sh` has something to report, a one-line band above the prompt says so until the cause is gone:

`containers: disk 14 GB free, floor 20 · 2 dangling images · 1 volume of a gone worktree · 21 buildah (any project) — /containers`

**Why this priority**: the report today is a toast and a model-only line; by the time a build is interrupted again the person has forgotten it, which is how 21 buildah working containers (any project) piled up in this machine's store.

**Independent Test**: a `claude plugin test plugins/devcontainer` case mocks `$.process.run` for `leftovers.sh --json` with a recorded JSON stdout and mounts the band on `terminal` and `desktop`; it asserts the text by key. A second answer with `findings: []` asserts the band draws nothing.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the JSON holds a `dangling` and a `volumes` finding, **When** the band draws, **Then** it reads "containers: 2 dangling images · 1 volume of a gone worktree — /containers".
2. **Given** a `disk` finding, **When** drawn, **Then** the band leads with `disk 14 GB free, floor 20` (the script's own order), the text carries a `⚠` mark as well as any colour (the test asserts text by key, not colour), and "don't start parallel builders" is left to `/containers`.
3. **Given** `findings: []` (all clean) **or** `checked: false`, **When** refreshed, **Then** the band draws nothing; for `checked: false` the reason is kept in state for `/containers` to report.
4. **Given** a model turn running (`isWorking`) or a survey (`hasSurvey`), **When** the band would draw, **Then** it yields.
5. **Given** a finding with a `kind` the mod doesn't know (a newer script), **When** drawn, **Then** the band shows `<kind> <count>` from the JSON, never nothing and never a guess; a JSON that doesn't parse shows nothing and `/containers` says the report was unreadable.

---

### User Story 2 - `/containers` prints the whole report (Priority: P2)

`/containers` prints the findings (one line each, from the JSON) and the script's text form (run without `--json`) when the person wants the script's own advice, and a pointer: "`wt.py resources` lists them with sizes (agents:parallel); removal is by ID or by this project's label (containers.md §9a) and asks for anything that isn't this project's". It is output, not a model turn, and removes nothing.

**Independent Test**: raise `command.run` for `containers` with the script mocked; assert the text, that no other process was started, and that the text contains no prune command.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** two findings, **When** `/containers` runs, **Then** both lines appear in the script's words followed by the pointer.
2. **Given** `findings: []`, **When** it runs, **Then** it says "no leftovers or disk problem reported for this project".
3. **Given** `checked: false`, **When** it runs, **Then** it says nothing was checked and gives the script's `reason` (`no-engine`, `not-a-checkout` or `disabled`), no guessing.

---

### User Story 3 - Fresh after container work (Priority: P2)

The band is read again at session start, after a Bash call that built, ran or removed container resources, and on `turn.complete` at most every two minutes.

**Independent Test**: a `tool.call` for `podman build -t x .` completes with the script mocked to a new answer; assert one extra read and the new text. A call for `ls` triggers none.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a completed call whose command starts with `podman`/`docker`/`buildah` and `build`, `run`, `rm`, `rmi`, `volume`, `compose`, or with `wt.py` (`add`, `remove`, `finish`), **When** it finishes, **Then** the band is read again once.
2. **Given** `wt.py finish` removed the dangling images, **When** the next read finds nothing, **Then** the band disappears.
3. **Given** two such calls within a second, **When** they finish, **Then** one read runs (the second joins the first).

### Edge Cases

- **No engine, no git checkout, script missing**: the band draws nothing; `/containers` says the reason the JSON gave, or that the script was missing.
- **A slow engine**: the script runs under `$.process.run` with a 10 s timeout (its hook timeout); on timeout the previous text stays and `/containers` says it timed out.
- **Other projects' buildah containers**: the script counts the whole store ("any project"); the band says `(any project)` and never offers removal; `wt.py baseline` and `wt.py finish` (agents) are what attribute and remove only the new ones.
- **Inside a worktree** (`.worktrees/<slug>`): the script computes the project from the main checkout's git common dir, so the band is the same in each.
- **Refresh cost**: the script runs a few engine calls (`images`, `volume ls`, one `volume inspect` per labelled volume, `ps -a --external`); the throttle and the trigger list keep it off every turn; never a timer while idle.
- **Narrow terminal**: one line sized to `e.props.bodyColumns`; under 60 columns it shortens to `containers ⚠ 3 — /containers`.
- **Non-terminal surfaces**: `AbovePrompt` is drawn where it exists; `/containers` prints text everywhere.
- **Two bands** (checkpoint, hygiene): composes beneath like 017's (`await next(e)` first).
- **Hot reload**: the last text and its read time live in `$.state`; the session-start toast is not repeated.
- **Headless (`claude -p`)**: no band; `/containers` still answers text.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The band's findings MUST come from `leftovers.sh --json`, read through `$.process.run` of the plugin's own script; the mod MUST NOT run an engine command of its own and MUST NOT compute a leftover, size or disk figure.
- **FR-002**: The mod MUST NOT remove, stop, build or pull anything, and no text it draws or prints MAY teach a prune; removal hints are only the script's own (by ID or by this project's label, `shared/containers.md` §9a). A test asserts no band or `/containers` text matches `prune`, and `scripts/consistency.py`'s prune check stays green.
- **FR-003**: Findings MUST be read from the JSON's `kind`, `count`, `free_gb` and `floor_gb` keys (pinned by `scripts/consistency.py`); the mod MUST NOT parse the script's sentences. An unknown `kind` is shown as `<kind> <count>`.
- **FR-004**: `AI_GENT_NO_LEFTOVERS_CHECK=1` silences the band as it silences the script (the mod adds no check of its own).
- **FR-005**: The refresh triggers MUST be: `session.start` (detached, like 014's, so the start isn't held), a completed Bash call whose command starts with a container engine and one of the verbs above or with `wt.py`, and `turn.complete` at most once per `containersRefreshSeconds`.
- **FR-006**: `userConfig`: `containersBand` (boolean, default true), `containersRefreshSeconds` (number, default 120), `containersCommand` (boolean, default true); the existing `leftoversToast` is unchanged.
- **FR-007**: The prerequisite change adds `--json` to `leftovers.sh` and its cases to `scripts/test-containers-guard.sh`; the default text output, `wt.py` and `shared/containers.md` are unchanged.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `claude plugin test plugins/devcontainer` passes: stories 1–3 on `terminal` and `desktop`, the empty answer, an unrecognized line, the trigger list, the throttle.
- **SC-002**: `scripts/test-containers-guard.sh` passes, with its existing text cases unchanged and the new `--json` cases added.
- **SC-003**: On this machine, with its 21 buildah working containers in the store, the band appears within one refresh and says `21 buildah (any project)`; after `wt.py finish` removes the ones new since a baseline, the next refresh shows the remainder, and it stays absent when the store is clean.

## Out of scope

- Removing anything, offering a button to, or suggesting a prune (§9a).
- Sizes per resource (`wt.py resources` and `system df` do that).
- Disk figures beyond the script's below-floor line; other engines' stores.
- Changing the floor (`wt.py`'s `settings` and §9a own it).

## Decisions (2026-10-31, with the maintainer)

- The band reads `leftovers.sh` rather than `wt.py resources --json`: the script is in the same plugin (`$.plugin.root` points at it, as `plugins/secrets/hooks/register.tsx` reads its own `references/`; 015 R4 shows imports stop at the plugin's edge), while `wt.py` lives in `plugins/agents/scripts/` and `devcontainer` has no recorded way to find it.
- `leftovers.sh` gains `--json` as its own change, landed before the mod, so the mod never parses its sentences; `scripts/test-containers-guard.sh` gains the cases and `consistency.py` pins the shape. `--json` always prints an object when the script ran (`findings` empty when clean) and `{checked: false, reason}` when it could not check.
- The session-start toast stays beside the band: it reaches the person at the moment of attention, the band is what remains; turn the toast off with `leftoversToast` if the band is enough. This feature supersedes 017's FR-005 "never run a second time" for the band's own reads.
- The band's order follows the script's: disk, dangling images, volumes, buildah.
- `/containers` is a plain `/<name>` command (017's rule for `/release-preview`).

- Band priority (030): the band records itself in the `devcontainer` plugin's `bands` atom, `normal` while a `disk` finding is present and `info` for leftovers alone, because the spec declared none; it registers no `/bands` command (git and project do).

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: `$.process.run` passes the session's environment to the script, so `CONTAINER_ENGINE` and `AI_GENT_NO_LEFTOVERS_CHECK` apply as they do for the hook.]
- [ASSUMPTION: the JSON keys listed in the ground rules are the contract; `scripts/consistency.py` fails if the script's keys and the mod's differ (plan, task 2).]
- [ASSUMPTION: the engine lets a Bash `tool.call` hook read the command after `next(e)`, as 017's `MOVES_REFS` hook does.]

# Feature Specification: Secret warning and redaction for tool output

**Feature Branch**: `docs/mod-specs-2` (specification only; built on its own branch)

**Created**: 2026-10-31

**Status**: Implemented

**Input**: A Claude Code mod that tells the person when a tool's result looks like it holds a credential — a `cat .env`, an `env` dump, a log line, a fetched page, a `Read` of a credentials file — using the same value patterns the prompt mask uses, says what to do (rotate it, and keep the new one in pass under `ai-gent/<area>/<name>`), and, for the results of `Bash` and `WebFetch`, **replaces the matched value with a placeholder in the stored row**, so neither the model nor the transcript file reads it. It is a last line of defense for what the secrets guard (which keeps `pass` values out) and the prompt mask (which covers what the person types) can't see. For other tools (`Read`, `Grep`, MCP) it warns and leaves the result intact.

**Depends on**: 016 (secret mask) — `shared/secret-patterns.json`, `plugins/secrets/hooks/secret-mask.ts`, the module and its generated `secret-data.ts`; 012 (checkpoint mod) — layout, `check.sh` wiring, versioning and install.

## Context and ground rules

- **The gap.** `shared/secrets.md` says a secret is never "pasted into the conversation" or put "in the agent's shell environment", and 016 masks what the person sends; it lists tool results as out of scope ("Masking tool results or model output (`session.append`, `process.spawn`); a later feature could reuse the same patterns"). The `secrets` guard (`plugins/secrets/hooks/guard.sh`) denies commands that would show a value from pass, but a value can still arrive in a result: a repository's `.env`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `printenv`, a test log, a page.
- **The route (verified in the kit's types on 2026-10-31).** A hook on `session.append` with the matcher `{ door: 'tool-result' }` sees each tool-result row before it is stored. `next({ ...e, message })` rewrites the row's `content` — a `tool_result`'s `content` and `is_error`, text blocks — and "the model and the transcript file never read that form"; the screen, an SDK stream or Remote Control may show the original for an instant first. The row's `e.origin` is `{ kind: 'tool', tool }`, the tool's **name** (`unknown` when no call of that id is found); it carries no input, so the `Read` path or the command is **not** available to this hook. The same probe of `session.append{door=tool-result}`, `session.compact` and `$.session.usage` passed `claude plugin validate` on the CI pin, Claude Code 2.1.312 (2026-10-31); `claude plugin test` cases confirm the behavior at build time (R1).
- **What redaction can and can't do.** It stops the value reaching the model's next request and the transcript. It cannot recall what already happened: the tool ran, the screen may have drawn the original, the process may have written it elsewhere (a log, a file), and a value the person or a tool echoed in another row (a `Read` result) is another row. So the toast still says **the value should be treated as exposed** and to rotate it, and never says it was erased.
- **Why not every tool.** A model that reads a file and sees a placeholder where a value was may write the placeholder back into that file, corrupting it; `Read` and `Grep` results are file content the model acts on. The first cut therefore redacts `Bash` and `WebFetch` only (command output and fetched pages, where a value is least expected and nothing is edited from it) and, for every other tool (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, MCP tools), warns and leaves the row intact. Which tools redact is a `userConfig` list (FR-006), so a person can opt a tool out or in.
- **Never echo.** The toast, the debug log, `$.state` and every test failure message hold the **kind**, a **count** and the **tool's name**, never any part of the value: not a prefix, not the last four characters, not a hash. The placeholder itself carries only the kind: `<github-token>`.
- **Which patterns.** The 016 list, but only its **high-confidence** kinds: private keys, GitHub tokens, `sk-` keys, AWS access keys, Slack tokens and URL passwords. The `NAME=value` and `Bearer|Basic` kinds are left out of a result, as 016 leaves them out of a skill's body (`skipIn`), because results are full of prose, examples and code (`Basic authentication`, `DB_PASSWORD=<value>`). A planned `skipIn: ["result"]` on those two patterns expresses it.
- **What the pre-filter must not break.** `scripts`, tests and docs in this repository hold token-shaped fixtures built from fragments (`shared/secret-cases.json`); a `Bash` result that prints such a fixture is redacted like any other, which is acceptable (the fragments themselves don't match).
- Owner: the `secrets` plugin; its module `plugins/secrets/hooks/register.tsx` (shared with 015's and 016's parts).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - A leaked credential in a Bash or WebFetch result is flagged and redacted (Priority: P1)

The agent runs `cat .env` and the output holds `AKIA` + 16 characters. The row the model reads shows `<aws-key>` where the value was, and a toast says: "output-secret: the result of Bash held 1 AWS key — redacted in what Claude reads; treat it as exposed anyway: rotate it with AWS, then keep the new one in pass (`secrets:pass`)."

**Why this priority**: a credential in a result reaches the model and the transcript with nothing in the way, and the person often isn't watching the output scroll by.

**Independent Test**: a `claude plugin test plugins/secrets` case raises `session.append` with `door: 'tool-result'`, `origin: { kind: 'tool', tool: 'Bash' }` and a `tool_result` block whose text holds a fixture per kind (assembled from fragments at run time, 016's rule), and asserts that the row passed to `next` holds the placeholder and none of the fixture, that one toast names kind, count and tool, and that no output holds a fragment of the fixture.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a `Bash` result holding `ghp_` followed by 36 letters, **When** the row is appended, **Then** the stored row holds `<github-token>` in its place, and one toast says 1 GitHub token, that it was redacted in what Claude reads, to treat it as exposed, to rotate it and to run `pass insert ai-gent/github/pat` — the entry in `shared/secret-patterns.json`.
2. **Given** a kind with no entry in the patterns file (AWS, `sk-`, Slack, URL password, private key), **When** flagged, **Then** the toast says to rotate it at the service that issued it and points at `secrets:pass` and `shared/secrets.md`'s section "Entry names", naming no invented entry.
3. **Given** a result holding two tokens and a URL password, **When** flagged, **Then** all three are replaced, and one toast lists all kinds with counts (never one toast per match).
4. **Given** a result with `DB_PASSWORD=<value>` or `Bearer authentication`, **When** appended, **Then** the row is unchanged and nothing is shown (the low-confidence kinds don't apply to results).
5. **Given** a result that matches nothing, **When** appended, **Then** the row is passed on byte for byte unchanged and nothing is shown.
6. **Given** `secretOutputWarning` off, **When** a leaked token appears, **Then** the row is unchanged and nothing is shown.
7. **Given** a `WebFetch` result holding a Slack token, **When** appended, **Then** it is redacted like a `Bash` result.

---

### User Story 2 - Other tools get the warning, never a rewrite (Priority: P1)

A `Read` of `~/.aws/credentials` or a `Grep` that hits a key returns a result holding a credential. The row is left exactly as the tool returned it (so a later `Edit` of that file stays correct), and the toast says: "output-secret: the result of Read held 1 AWS key — it was not redacted (file content the agent may edit); treat it as exposed: rotate it…".

**Independent Test**: the same case with `origin.tool` `Read`, `Grep` and an MCP tool name asserts the row is unchanged and the toast text says "not redacted" and holds no fragment of the value.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a `Read` result with a token, **When** appended, **Then** the stored row equals the received row and one toast says it was not redacted.
2. **Given** `secretOutputTools` listing `Read`, **When** the same result arrives, **Then** it is redacted like a `Bash` result (the person's choice, documented as risking a placeholder written back into a file).
3. **Given** `origin.tool` is `unknown`, **When** a token is found, **Then** the row is left unchanged and the toast names the tool as `unknown` (the mod never redacts a row whose tool it can't name).

---

### User Story 3 - Quiet when it repeats (Priority: P2)

Reading the same `.env` five times, or a log with fifty tokens, must not bury the person in toasts. (Redaction still happens every time; only the toasts are rate-limited.)

**Independent Test**: raise six appended rows with matching results inside a minute; assert every row is redacted (or left, per tool), at most three toasts and one final summary toast, never a toast per row.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the same kind flagged in the same turn by two rows, **When** the second is appended, **Then** it joins the first toast's count instead of raising another.
2. **Given** more than three warnings in a minute, **When** another matches, **Then** it is counted, and one summary toast ("N more results held credentials this session — treat them as exposed too") is shown once, with no value in it.

### Edge Cases

- **Images, PDFs and binary results**: not scanned and never rewritten (a hook may drop or move media blocks but not change them, per the types); text blocks and a `tool_result`'s text `content` only.
- **Very large results**: the scan stops after the first 256 KiB of a result's text; the rest is passed on unscanned and the toast says "scanned the first 256 KiB" if it did. A cheap substring pre-filter (`BEGIN`, `gh`, `github_pat_`, `sk-`, `AKIA`, `xox`, `://`) skips results that can't match. The pre-filter is a new `LOOKS.result` entry: `secret-mask.ts` declares `LOOKS: Record<Scope, RegExp>` (line 78), so adding `'result'` to `Scope` fails to compile until the table has its entry.
- **Redaction itself fails** (the compiled patterns throw, or the rewritten row is refused): decided 2026-10-31 (the maintainer accepted the default): **fail open** — the row is stored as received through the hook's `.catch` replaying `next(e)`, and a loud toast says "output-secret: could not check or redact this result — treat any credential in it as exposed". A failed scan loses a row's protection, never the row.
- **Results of the secrets plugin's own commands**: `pass ls` and the like show names only; nothing special is needed.
- **Fixtures and docs in a repository**: a `Read` of `shared/secret-cases.json` shows fragments, which don't match; a token-shaped example in a `Read` result is flagged and left intact (a warning costs a glance); in a `Bash` result it is redacted, and `secretOutputWarning` or the tool list can turn that off.
- **The person pasted the token and the agent echoed it back**: 016 already masked the input, so an echo carries the mask, not the value.
- **Headless (`claude -p`)**: the toast goes to the debug log with kind and count only; redaction still applies.
- **Narrow terminal**: the toast is one line; the rotate/pass hint is also in the transcript notice if it doesn't fit.
- **Hot reload**: patterns are compiled once (016's `loadRules`); the toast-rate counters live in `$.state` and reset with the session.
- **Subagents' results**: a row's `agentId` is carried unchanged; a subagent's tool-result rows are handled the same way.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The mod MUST hook `session.append` with `{ door: 'tool-result' }`, scan the row's text content, and for a row whose `origin.tool` is in the redact list replace each match of a high-confidence kind with `<kind>` through `next({ ...e, message })`; for every other row it MUST pass the row on unchanged. A row with no match MUST be passed on unchanged and untouched.
- **FR-002**: Patterns MUST come from `shared/secret-patterns.json` through 016's `compile`, using only the kinds not marked `skipIn: ["result"]`; no pattern is copied into the module. `secret-mask.ts`'s `Scope` gains `'result'` and its `LOOKS` table gains the matching entry (decided in the plan: `LOOKS.result` holds the pre-filter, so `looksSecret` works for results too).
- **FR-003**: The toast, the debug log, `$.state` and test output MUST hold only kinds, counts and the tool's name (from `e.origin.tool`), never any part of a match and never a `Read` path or a command (the row does not carry them); tests assert it on every kind.
- **FR-004**: The toast MUST say the value is to be treated as exposed, to rotate it, and where its replacement belongs (the entry from the patterns file when there is one, otherwise `secrets:pass` and `shared/secrets.md`); for a redacted row it says "redacted in what Claude reads", for an unredacted one "not redacted", and it MUST NOT say or imply the value was erased or that nothing was exposed.
- **FR-005**: At most one toast per appended row, at most three per minute, then a single summary; the rate limit never skips a redaction.
- **FR-006**: `userConfig`: `secretOutputWarning` (boolean, default true) turns the whole feature off; `secretOutputRedact` (boolean, default true) turns redaction off (warn-only); `secretOutputTools` (a comma-separated list of tool names, default `Bash,WebFetch`) names the tools whose results are redacted — the per-tool opt-out and opt-in. A tool not listed is warn-only. [If `userConfig` takes no string type on the pin, two booleans `secretOutputRedactBash` and `secretOutputRedactWebFetch` replace the list; R4 verifies.]
- **FR-007**: The mod MUST NOT write `$.store` or files, and MUST NOT call a model or the network.
- **FR-008**: `shared/secret-patterns.json` gains the optional `skipIn` value `"result"` on `assignment` and `auth-header`, with `sessions.py`'s output unchanged and `secret-data.ts` regenerated (`python3 scripts/consistency.py --sync-secret-data`).
- **FR-009**: On any failure of the scan or the rewrite the hook MUST fail open (the row stored as received) with the loud toast of the edge case; it MUST NOT drop or delay a row.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `claude plugin test plugins/secrets` passes with: one redaction fixture per high-confidence kind for `Bash` and `WebFetch`; the same fixtures left intact (with a toast) for `Read`, `Grep` and an MCP tool name; no-match; the two low-confidence kinds (silent); `unknown` tool (left intact); large-result; repeat-limit; a throwing scan (row stored as received, loud toast); `secretOutputRedact` off; the tool list changed; and a no-value-in-any-output check.
- **SC-002**: `python3 -m unittest plugins/project/scripts/test_scripts.py` (the redaction cases) and `scripts/test-secrets-guard.sh` pass. Adding `'result'` to the data does not change `sessions.py`'s output; if `plugins/project/scripts/test_scripts.py`'s scope handling (it knows only `skill` today, near line 190) needs a case for the new `skipIn` value, that is a small additive test change recorded in the plan, not a change to existing cases.
- **SC-003**: A check in `scripts/consistency.py` fails if `secret-data.ts` differs from the patterns and cases (the existing whole-file equality check, `check_secret_data`, already covers `skipIn` because the twin is generated from the JSON); the plan adds a case in `scripts/test_consistency.py` that a `skipIn: ["result"]` entry survives the regeneration.

## Out of scope

- Redacting `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` or MCP results by default (listed in `secretOutputTools` only by the person's choice), erasing a transcript row already written, or rotating a credential: rotation is the person's, at the service.
- Detecting arbitrary high-entropy strings or names like `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in prose.
- Stopping the tool before it runs (that's the guard's job, and it can't know what a file holds).
- Changing `plugins/secrets/hooks/guard.sh`, `shared/secrets.md`'s rules, or 016's masking.

## Decisions (2026-10-31, with the maintainer)

- The mod warns and redacts: a `session.append` hook on `door: 'tool-result'` replaces the matched value with a `<kind>` placeholder in the stored row, which neither the model nor the transcript file reads in its original form. The screen may show the original for an instant (types of Claude Code 2.1.316; the events passed `claude plugin validate` on the 2.1.312 pin). The first draft's warn-only `tool.call` route is dropped; hiding the result from the model is in the first cut, no longer projected.
- **First cut redacts `Bash` and `WebFetch` only.** `Read`, `Grep` and every other tool get the toast and are left intact so file edits stay correct (a placeholder read from a file could be written back into it). The list is a `userConfig` option (FR-006).
- High-confidence kinds only, via a new `skipIn` value `result`, so the one shared list stays the single source.
- Never a hash or fingerprint of a match: repeats are limited by count and rate, not by remembering values.
- The toast still says to treat the value as exposed and to rotate it, and never shows any part of a match.
- **decided 2026-10-31 (the maintainer accepted the default): if redaction itself fails, fail open** with a loud toast, rather than hold the row back (holding a row back could break a tool run).

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: a `session.append` row for a tool result carries the tool's name in `e.origin.tool` (the 2.1.316 types say so, `unknown` when the call isn't found) and its text in the `tool_result` block's `content`; on 2.1.312 only the hook's registration is validated, so a `claude plugin test` case checks the origin and content shape first (plan, task 1; R1).]
- [ASSUMPTION: the hook sees `WebFetch` and MCP results as well as `Bash`, `Read` and `Grep`; if a tool's rows don't arrive by this door, the spec says which tools are covered.]
- [ASSUMPTION: `userConfig` accepts a string option; otherwise two booleans (FR-006; R4).]
- Fallback if `e.origin.tool` is absent on the pin: a `tool.call` hook (after `next`) records `tool_use_id` to tool name in an atom, and the `session.append` hook looks the tool up by the `tool_use_id` its `tool_result` block carries; the Bash/WebFetch split then does not depend on `origin`. Found 2026-10-31: the 2.1.312 pin already runs `session.append` hooks (the installed `git` and `devcontainer` mods register them), and `claude plugin validate` accepts `userConfig` options of `type: string` there. A headless `claude -p --plugin-dir` run does not load a hooks module, so the `origin` shape needs an interactive session or a `claude plugin test` case (plan task 1).

# Feature Specification: Next-stage prompt

**Feature Branch**: `docs/mod-specs-2` (specification only; built on its own branch)

**Created**: 2026-10-31

**Status**: Implemented

**Input**: A Claude Code mod that, when a pipeline stage writes its artifact (a brief, an architecture, a `specs/README.md`, a feature's `tasks.md`), toasts the next stage to run, reusing the pipeline pane's recommendation instead of a second set of rules. Grounded in `plugins/project/skills/status/SKILL.md` §4, `shared/pipeline.md`, and `plugins/project/hooks/pipeline-model.ts` (`recommend`, `ARTIFACTS`) and `pipeline.ts` (`compute`, whose snapshot already carries `next`).

**Depends on**: 013 (pipeline pane) — `recommend`, `compute` and the artifact list; 012 for the module. Implemented.

## Context and ground rules

- A mod is an optional, Claude Code-only layer. `project:status` stays the report of record and `shared/pipeline.md` the contract; the toast is a hint that names a stage and the reason, and it never runs the stage, fills the prompt or submits anything.
- It adds no rules. The recommendation is the snapshot's `next` (`compute($).next`, which is `recommend(artifacts, features, markers.items)` from `pipeline-model.ts`, `pipeline.ts:158`), so 013 and 027 cannot disagree; a change to the rules is a change there, with its parity test. What `recommend` returns is what the toast says, including `/project:status` when no rule fires.
- Owner: the `project` plugin; code beside 013's, composed from `register.tsx`. It works whether the pane is open or not.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Told what comes next when a stage finishes (Priority: P1)

After a stage writes `specs/README.md` with a feature that needs planning, a toast reads `specs index written — next: /project:spec (001-foo needs plan)`. After `project:init` writes only `docs/product/brief.md`, `recommend` returns no rule (rule 2's "missing" needs a later artifact to exist, `pipeline-model.ts:175-206`) and the toast reads `brief written — next: /project:status (nothing is ready to start; the full report covers QA, docs and CI)`.

**Why this priority**: a stage ends with the model saying what is next; the person who stepped away, or a headless run, never sees it. The pane shows it only when open.

**Independent Test**: a `claude plugin test` case mounts the module on a fixture tree from `pipeline-fixtures.ts`, raises an Edit/Write completion on `specs/README.md` with `$.fs` answering the new tree, and asserts one toast whose stage and reason equal the snapshot's `next`, on `terminal` and `desktop`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a Write to a path in `ARTIFACTS` (or under `specs/NNN-*/`) that was absent before, **When** the call completes, **Then** the snapshot is recomputed with `compute($)` and, when its `next` differs from the one recorded, a toast names the artifact written, the recommended stage and its reason.
2. **Given** the recommended stage is the same as before the write, **When** it completes, **Then** no toast (nothing new to say).
3. **Given** an Edit that only changes an existing artifact, **When** it completes, **Then** no toast unless the recommended stage changed.
4. **Given** the recommendation is rule 1 (an open `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`), **When** a write creates it, **Then** the toast says `ask the user` with `file:line`, as the pane does.
5. **Given** no rule fires (`next.rule` is null, `stage` is `/project:status`, "nothing is ready to start"), **When** a write completes, **Then** one toast says so, once, and points to `/project:status`.
6. **Given** the session just started, **When** the first watched write completes, **Then** "the one before" is the `next` recorded at session start (`nextStageLast`, seeded by a detached `compute` that toasts nothing), so the first change is judged against something.
7. **Given** an Edit adds a `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` and no artifact appears, **When** it completes and `next` becomes rule 1, **Then** the toast says `ask the user` with `file:line` (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-31).

---

### User Story 2 - One toast per change, not a stream (Priority: P1)

During a build stage that writes many files under `specs/`, the person is not toasted for each.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** ten Writes under `specs/004-x/` in one turn, **When** the turn completes, **Then** at most one toast, for the final recommendation, if it differs from the one before the turn.
2. **Given** a toast was shown for a stage, **When** the same stage is recommended again later with the same reason, **Then** it is not repeated within the session.

---

### User Story 3 - Off switch and surfaces (Priority: P3)

`nextStageToast` is a `userConfig` boolean (default true), shown in `/config`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `nextStageToast` off, **When** a stage writes an artifact, **Then** nothing is computed.
2. **Given** a headless run (`claude -p`), **When** a stage writes an artifact, **Then** nothing shows (a toast has no surface); the module registers nothing that draws.

### Edge Cases

- **No pipeline project** (no `docs/product/`, no `specs/`): nothing runs; the first-write case (the brief itself) is the one that starts the pipeline and does toast.
- **Cost**: `compute` lists and stats the artifacts and reads or spawns only what changed by `mtimeMs` (`pipeline.ts:28-45`: `markersByFile`, `dateByPath`, `readme` are module-level caches, so `compute` is read-only toward the project but not free of module state; a reload empties them and the next call refills). It runs only on a write to a watched path, at most once per turn.
- **The pane is open**: 013's existing `tool.call` Edit/Write hook (`register.tsx:158-166`) already refreshes the snapshot atom on a path containing `/docs/product/` or `/specs/`; 027 extends that hook (one trigger, not a second hook) and reuses the atom's snapshot when `computedAt` is newer than the write, and recomputes otherwise.
- **Writes by another tool** (a Bash redirect, a script, `specsync.py`): not seen as tool writes; the turn-complete check compares `mtimeMs` of the watched paths and covers them (at most one `stat` per path).
- **Orchestrated runs** (`agents:orchestrate`, `agents:parallel`): many writers; the once-per-turn rule applies and the toast names only the final recommendation.
- **Hot reload**: the last recommendation and the shown set live in `$.state` atoms.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The mod MUST NOT write any file, run a stage, fill or submit a prompt; it only toasts text.
- **FR-002**: The recommendation MUST be `compute($).next` from `pipeline.ts` (that is `recommend()` from `pipeline-model.ts`); a second implementation of `project:status` §4 is forbidden, and the mod never calls `recommend` separately.
- **FR-003**: A toast MUST fire only when the recommended stage or reason differs from the last one recorded, and at most once per turn.
- **FR-004**: It MUST label itself a hint and point to `/project:status` for the full report, as the pane does.
- **FR-005**: It MUST do nothing while `nextStageToast` is false, without touching 012's or 013's parts of the module.
- **FR-006**: Triggers MUST be limited to the paths the existing Edit/Write hook matches (`e.file_path` containing `/docs/product/` or `/specs/`, 013's watched set), plus an `mtimeMs` check at turn end. The mod extends that hook rather than adding a second `tool.call` hook for the same tools.
- **FR-007**: The mod MUST seed `nextStageLast` at `session.start` with a detached `compute` that raises no toast.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `claude plugin test plugins/project` passes, with stories 1–3 on `terminal` and `desktop`.
- **SC-002**: For each of the pane's rule fixtures (`pipeline-fixtures.ts`), the toast's stage and reason equal the snapshot's `next`, including the no-rule case (`/project:status`).
- **SC-003**: Ten writes in one turn produce one toast.
- **SC-004**: `claude plugin validate plugins/project` reports no refusal.

## Out of scope

- Running or queuing the next stage; filling the prompt (the pane's Next button does that on press; a toast has no button).
- Changing the recommendation rules, `project:status`, or `shared/pipeline.md`.
- A native notification (`$.ui.notify`): a toast is enough for a hint.
- Other agents (opencode, Codex, …).

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: `compute($)` writes nothing to the project or to atoms (it reads and refills its module caches; `refresh` writes the atom), as `pipeline.ts` has it today.]
- [ASSUMPTION: Claude Code 2.1.312's `tool.call` Edit/Write payload carries `file_path`, as 013 already reads it.]

## Decisions (2026-10-31, with the maintainer)

- Toast also on an edit that adds a `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` with no new artifact. No session-start toast (that is `project:status`).
- Truthful examples: the toast quotes what `snapshot.next` holds. Writing only the brief yields `/project:status`, not `/project:architecture`, because 013's rule 2 reports a missing artifact only when a later stage's artifact exists. Changing that would be a change to 013's rules and `project:status` §4 (out of scope here).
- `compute($).next` is used; `recommend` is not called separately. The trigger extends 013's existing Edit/Write hook (`register.tsx:158-166`).
- `nextStageLast` is seeded at session start without a toast (decided 2026-10-31 (the maintainer accepted the default): the alternative is to treat the first change of a session as always worth a toast).
- Should the brief-only case say `/project:architecture` anyway (a rule change in 013 and `project:status`)? decided 2026-10-31 (the maintainer accepted the default): no; keep one source of rules.
- Built (2026-10-31): the Edit/Write hook only notes the write; the one toast speaks at `turn.complete`, so ten writes give one toast for the final recommendation. The hook awaits the detached session-start seed before the call runs, so the seed reads the tree as it was. The Edit/Write hook now registers even with `pipelinePane` off, so the toast does not depend on the pane.

# Feature Specification: Release readiness band

**Feature Branch**: `docs/mod-specs-2` (specification only; built on its own branch)

**Created**: 2026-10-31

**Status**: Implemented

**Input**: A Claude Code mod that keeps the next release in view: a band above the prompt saying what `scripts/release.py --dry-run --json` would do now (`next: 2.23.0 (minor) · 3 plugins bump`), so the person sees, before promoting to `main`, whether the commits since the last tag release anything. It extends 017's `/release-preview` by showing the same plan without a command. Grounded in `scripts/release.py` and `shared/release-single.py` (their plan and exit codes; both gain `--json`, Planned) and `plugins/git/hooks/hygiene.ts` (`releasePreview`).

**Depends on**: 012 (checkpoint mod) — module layout; 017 (repo hygiene) — the git module, `releasePreview`, the `AbovePrompt` composition and the ref-moving refresh. Implemented.

## Context and ground rules

- A mod is an optional, Claude Code-only layer. `scripts/release.py` and `.github/workflows/release.yml` stay the only things that release; the band runs the script with `--dry-run --json` only (`releasePreview` runs it with `--dry-run`) and never without `--dry-run`. The new `--json` flag is an error without `--dry-run` (`parser.error`, exit 2), so it cannot release. It never fetches, pulls, commits, tags or pushes, and does not decide whether to promote: that is `git:workflow`, asked first.
- It reads only what the script prints as JSON (the shape is in `data-model.md`) and exit code 3 for "no release needed". The mod computes no version or bump of its own and parses no prose.
- Owner: the `git` plugin; code beside `hygiene.ts`, composed from `register.tsx`. It applies only where `scripts/release.py` exists (this repository, and projects set up from `shared/release-single.py`), and only when HEAD is a chain branch (`CHAIN` in `hygiene-model.ts`: `main`, `master`, `dev`, `develop`; the maintainer's wording is "dev or main").
- The band is one of the bands above the prompt and obeys the band-priority rule (at most two visible, holds and failures first; specified separately, Planned). Its priority is `info`, the lowest: it yields to a checkpoint hold (012), a failing CI run (023) and 017's unpulled-release band.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - See what the next release would be (Priority: P1)

When commits since the last tag are releasable, a band reads `next release 2.23.0 (minor, since 2.22.0) · 3 plugins bump — /release-preview for the plan`. When nothing is releasable, no band is drawn.

**Why this priority**: it answers "would promoting now release anything, and what" without a command, and shows when a docs-only run of commits will not (CLAUDE.md "Releases").

**Independent Test**: a `claude plugin test` case mocks `$.process.run` to answer `release.py --dry-run` with a recorded plan on stdout (exit 0) and mounts the band on `terminal` and `desktop`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the dry run exits 0 with JSON `{version: "2.23.0", bump: "minor", since: "2.22.0", targets: [three of kind "plugin"]}`, **When** the band draws, **Then** it shows the version, the bump kind, the base tag and the plugin count.
2. **Given** exit code 3, **When** drawn, **Then** no band (nothing releasable).
3. **Given** exit code 1 or 2, a start failure, or stdout that is not the expected JSON, **When** drawn, **Then** a single dim line says the preview failed, with the script's first stderr line (the script prints `release.py: error: …` there), and does not retry until HEAD changes.
4. **Given** no `scripts/release.py`, **When** the session starts, **Then** nothing runs and nothing shows.
5. **Given** HEAD is a feature branch (not in `CHAIN`), **When** the session starts or a turn completes, **Then** the script is not run and no band is drawn (the dry run reads HEAD's history, so a feature branch's plan is not the next release).
6. **Given** `targets` holds no `plugin` entry (a project set up from `shared/release-single.py`: one `source` target), **When** the band draws, **Then** it omits the plugin count (`next release 1.4.0 (minor, since 1.3.2)`).

---

### User Story 2 - It stays current, cheaply (Priority: P1)

The dry run runs again only when HEAD or the tags merged into it changed, never on a timer.

**Independent Test**: advance the mocked clock and raise turn completions; assert the script ran once per distinct HEAD.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the band shown for HEAD `abc` and tags `T`, **When** a turn completes with HEAD still `abc` and the same tags, **Then** the script is not run again.
2. **Given** a Bash `git commit`, `git merge`, `git pull`, `git checkout`/`switch` or `git tag` completes (017's `MOVES_REFS` plus `tag`), **When** it finishes, **Then** HEAD and the merged tag list are read again and the script runs only if either changed.
3. **Given** a new tag from a release pulled in, **When** HEAD moved to it, **Then** the band updates (usually to none).

---

### User Story 3 - Open the full plan, and turn it off (Priority: P3)

The band's text names `/release-preview`, which prints the full dry run (the changelog section included). `releaseBand` (boolean, default true) turns the band off; `/release-preview` stays governed by 017's `releasePreview`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `releaseBand` off, **When** commits change, **Then** the module runs nothing for it, and `/release-preview` still works.
2. **Given** the user presses Hide, **When** the prompt redraws, **Then** the band stays hidden until HEAD changes.

### Edge Cases

- **Hygiene band also shown** (unpulled release): both compose; when `main`/`dev` are behind their remote the preview is computed on stale history, so the band adds "(local branch is behind origin)" and never suggests a pull itself.
- **No tags yet**: the JSON's `since` is `null`; the band says "first release". The mod does not pass `--initial` (the script's default 0.1.0 applies, as in `releasePreview`).
- **Cost**: `release.py` runs several git commands; one run per distinct HEAD, with a 60 s timeout as `releasePreview` uses.
- **Working tree dirty or mid-rebase**: the script reads commits, not the tree; the band is unaffected, and a git failure shows the dim line.
- **Narrow terminal**: below `bodyColumns` 60, the band reads `next 2.23.0 (minor)`.
- **Hot reload**: the parsed plan, the key it was computed for (HEAD plus tags) and the hidden flag live in `$.state` atoms (`data-model.md`).
- **Script without `--json`** (an older `release-single.py` copy in another project): the run exits 2 (unknown argument); the band shows the dim failure line once and stops, and says to re-run `devsecops:pipeline` to refresh the script.
- **Release job running** (a push to `main` just made): until the bot commit lands and is pulled, the band may still show the pending version; 017's band is the one that says to pull.
- **Headless (`claude -p`)**: nothing draws; `/release-preview` still answers as text.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The mod MUST run `scripts/release.py` only with `--dry-run --json`, MUST NOT run it any other way, and MUST NOT fetch, pull, commit, tag or push.
- **FR-002**: The band's figures MUST come from the script's JSON (`data-model.md`) and exit code (3 = no release). `scripts/release.py` and `shared/release-single.py` MUST gain `--json` together as one prior change, with the same keys; `scripts/consistency.py` fails when their keys differ or when `release-model.ts`'s key list differs from them, and both release test scripts cover the flag.
- **FR-003**: The script MUST run at most once per distinct key (HEAD plus `git tag --list --merged HEAD`), only when HEAD is a chain branch, detached from `session.start`, with the 60 s timeout `releasePreview` uses.
- **FR-004**: The band MUST compose with the bands beneath (`AbovePrompt`), as 012 and 017 do, and MUST NOT draw while the model is working (`isWorking`) or a survey is open, as 017's band does.
- **FR-005**: `/release-preview`'s behavior (017) MUST be unchanged; the band reuses its runner (`releasePreview`'s script call) instead of a second one.
- **FR-006**: `releaseBand` MUST turn the band off without touching 017's band, toasts or `/release-preview`.
- **FR-007**: The band MUST declare its priority (`info`) to the band-priority rule and MUST NOT draw when two higher-priority bands are visible.
- **FR-008**: The plugin count MUST count only `targets` of kind `plugin`; a plan with none omits the count, and the `CHANGELOG.md` line is never a target.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: `claude plugin test plugins/git` passes, with stories 1–3 on `terminal` and `desktop`.
- **SC-002**: On this repository with releasable commits on `dev`, the band's version equals the first line of `scripts/release.py --dry-run` and `--dry-run --json`'s `version`; with only `docs:` commits, no band.
- **SC-003**: Over a 10-minute session with no new commits, the script runs at most once.
- **SC-004**: `claude plugin validate plugins/git` reports no refusal; `scripts/consistency.py` still passes with the added model file.

## Out of scope

- Releasing, tagging, promoting or opening the release PR (`git:workflow`, `repo:pr`; asked first).
- Changing the bump rules or the text plan of `scripts/release.py` and `shared/release-single.py`. Adding `--json` to both is in scope, as a prior change (plan task 1).
- Container image retagging and platform release objects (`shared/release-platforms.md`).
- Previewing on a remote or in CI.
- Other agents (opencode, Codex, …).

## Assumptions

- [ASSUMPTION: `scripts/release.py --dry-run` exits 3 when nothing is releasable (`NO_RELEASE`, `scripts/release.py:55`) and prints the plan to stdout; `--json` keeps both.]
- [ASSUMPTION: `release.py`'s last tag (`git tag --list --merged HEAD`, highest by version, `last_tag`, :90-92) is what the plan's `since` reports; the mod does not read the tag itself.]
- [ASSUMPTION: Claude Code 2.1.312's `AbovePrompt` props (`isWorking`, `hasSurvey`, `bodyColumns`) stay as 017 reads them.]

## Decisions (2026-10-31, with the maintainer)

- `release.py` and `shared/release-single.py` gain `--json` together, as one change before the mod (the bump rules live in both). The band reads the JSON, not the plan's text.
- Shown only when HEAD is a chain branch; the maintainer said `dev` or `main`, and the mod uses `CHAIN` (adds `master` and `develop`, the names 017 already treats as the chain).
- Key is HEAD plus the merged tag list, not `git describe` (review 2026-10-31: `release.py`'s `last_tag` takes the highest merged version, which `describe` can disagree with).
- Plugin count: only `kind: "plugin"` targets; `release-single.py` plans have one `source` target and no count. The CHANGELOG line is not a target.
- Priority `info`, lowest of the bands (decided 2026-10-31 (the maintainer accepted the default): the band-priority rule is specified in `specs/030-band-priority`).
- Engine pin: Claude Code 2.1.312's `AbovePrompt` props are as 017 reads them; nothing here needs a newer API.
- Verified 2026-10-31 by running it: `scripts/release.py --dry-run` exits 3 with `no release needed: no feat, fix, perf, refactor or breaking commits since 2.22.0` when nothing is releasable.
